source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Selected public verse labels match the pinned records. Complete original records, including annotations, are hashed.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated word-event formula.
verses.before: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps the embodied direction and named target.
verses.before: "Son of man, set your face against the Ammonites and prophesy against them.
verses.after: “Son of man, turn your face toward the Ammonites and prophesy against them.
verses.tsw_comparator: "Son of man, set your face against the Ammonites and prophesy against them.

verses.rationale: Preserves three occasions of gloating and both titles.
verses.before: Say to the Ammonites, 'Hear the word of the LORD GOD: Thus says the LORD GOD: Because you said "Aha!" against my sanctuary when it was defiled, and against the land of Israel when it was desolate, and against the house of Judah when they went into exile,
verses.after: Tell the Ammonites: Hear the word of the Lord GOD! This is what the Lord GOD says: You said ‘Aha!’ when my sanctuary was profaned, when Israel’s land was laid waste, and when the house of Judah went into exile.
verses.tsw_comparator: Say to the Ammonites, 'Hear the word of the LORD GOD: Thus says the LORD GOD: Because you said "Aha!" against my sanctuary when it was defiled, and against the land of Israel when it was desolate, and against the house of Judah when they went into exile,

verses.rationale: Makes the invaders clear without supplying an ethnicity.
verses.before: so, I am giving you to the people of the East as a possession. They will set their camps among you and make their dwellings in your midst. They will eat your fruit and drink your milk.
verses.after: So I am handing you over to the people of the east as their possession. They will pitch their camps among you and set up their dwellings there. They will eat your fruit and drink your milk.
verses.tsw_comparator: therefore, I am giving you to the people of the East as a possession. They will set their camps among you and make their dwellings in your midst. They will eat your fruit and drink your milk.

verses.rationale: Retains distinct animals and recognition refrain.
verses.before: I will make Rabbah a pasture for camels and the Ammonites a resting place for flocks. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
verses.after: I will make Rabbah a pasture for camels and Ammon a resting place for flocks. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I will make Rabbah a pasture for camels and the Ammonites a resting place for flocks. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the gestures tied to contemptuous joy.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD GOD: Because you have clapped your hands and stamped your feet and rejoiced with all the malice of your soul against the land of Israel,
verses.after: For this is what the Lord GOD says: You clapped your hands and stamped your feet, rejoicing over Israel’s land with all the contempt in your heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD GOD: Because you have clapped your hands and stamped your feet and rejoiced with all the malice of your soul against the land of Israel,

verses.rationale: Follows read-form plunder; retains accumulating threats.
verses.before: so, look, I have stretched out my hand against you and will give you as plunder to the nations. I will cut you off from the peoples and make you perish from the lands. I will destroy you, and you will know that I am the LORD.'"
verses.after: So I have stretched out my hand against you. I will give you as plunder to the nations, cut you off from the peoples, and make you disappear from the lands. I will destroy you. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: therefore, behold, I have stretched out my hand against you and will give you as plunder to the nations. I will cut you off from the peoples and make you perish from the lands. I will destroy you, and you will know that I am the LORD.'"

verses.rationale: Preserves both speakers and their taunt.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD GOD: Because Moab and Seir said, "Look, the house of Judah is like all the nations,"
verses.after: “This is what the Lord GOD says: Moab and Seir said, ‘Look, the house of Judah is just like every other nation.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD GOD: Because Moab and Seir said, "Behold, the house of Judah is like all the nations,"

verses.rationale: Keeps flank image and three named towns.
verses.before: so, look, I will open the shoulder of Moab from the cities, from its cities on the frontier, the glory of the country—Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim—
verses.after: So I am opening Moab’s flank, stripping away its frontier towns, the glory of the land: Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim.
verses.tsw_comparator: therefore, behold, I will open the shoulder of Moab from the cities, from its cities on the frontier, the glory of the country—Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim—

verses.rationale: Retains the unexpected repeated Ammon reference.
verses.before: to the sons of the East, along with the Ammonites, and I will give it as a possession, so that the Ammonites may not be remembered among the nations.
verses.after: I will give Moab to the people of the east as a possession, along with the Ammonites, so that the Ammonites will no longer be remembered among the nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: to the sons of the East, along with the Ammonites, and I will give it as a possession, so that the Ammonites may not be remembered among the nations.

verses.rationale: Preserves plural judgments and recognition.
verses.before: I will execute judgments upon Moab. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
verses.after: I will carry out judgments against Moab. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I will execute judgments upon Moab. Then they shall know that I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated vengeance and emphatic guilt.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD GOD: Because Edom acted out of vengeance against the house of Judah and has grievously offended in taking revenge upon them,
verses.after: “This is what the Lord GOD says: Edom took vengeance on the house of Judah and became deeply guilty by taking revenge on them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD GOD: Because Edom acted out of vengeance against the house of Judah and has grievously offended in taking revenge upon them,

verses.rationale: Keeps geographic reach and nonhuman losses.
verses.before: so, thus says the LORD GOD: I will stretch out my hand against Edom and will cut off humans and animals from it, and I will lay it waste; from Teman to Dedan they will fall by the sword.
verses.after: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I will stretch out my hand against Edom and cut off humans and animals from it. I will make it a waste from Teman onward; as far as Dedan they will fall by the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: therefore, thus says the LORD GOD: I will stretch out my hand against Edom and will cut off humans and animals from it, and I will lay it waste; from Teman to Dedan they shall fall by the sword.

verses.rationale: Makes Edom the final referent without softening agency.
verses.before: I will lay my vengeance upon Edom by the hand of my people Israel. And they will act in Edom according to my anger and my wrath, and they will know my vengeance, declares the LORD GOD.
verses.after: I will put my vengeance against Edom into the hands of my people Israel. They will act against Edom according to my anger and fury, and Edom will know my vengeance, declares the Lord GOD.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will lay my vengeance upon Edom by the hand of my people Israel. And they shall act in Edom according to my anger and my wrath, and they shall know my vengeance, declares the LORD GOD.

verses.rationale: Retains intensity and longstanding hostility.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD GOD: Because the Philistines acted in revenge and took vengeance with malice in their souls to destroy with everlasting enmity,
verses.after: “This is what the Lord GOD says: The Philistines acted in revenge, taking vengeance with contempt in their hearts, seeking destruction out of age-old hostility.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD GOD: Because the Philistines acted in revenge and took vengeance with malice in their souls to destroy with everlasting enmity,

verses.rationale: Keeps Cherethites distinct within the oracle.
verses.before: so, thus says the LORD GOD: Look, I will stretch out my hand against the Philistines and will cut off the Cherethites and destroy the remnant of the seacoast.
verses.after: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I am stretching out my hand against the Philistines. I will cut off the Cherethites and destroy the remnant along the seacoast.
verses.tsw_comparator: therefore, thus says the LORD GOD: Behold, I will stretch out my hand against the Philistines and will cut off the Cherethites and destroy the remnant of the seacoast.

verses.rationale: Retains vengeance as the stated recognition setting.
verses.before: I will execute great vengeance upon them with wrathful rebukes. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I lay my vengeance upon them."
verses.after: I will carry out great acts of vengeance against them, with furious punishments. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I bring my vengeance upon them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will execute great vengeance upon them with wrathful rebukes. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I lay my vengeance upon them."

verses.rationale: Does not invent the missing month number.
verses.before: Now it happened in the eleventh year, on the first of the month, that the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
verses.after: In the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: Now it came to pass in the eleventh year, on the first of the month, that the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps gateway and filling metaphors without economic expansion.
verses.before: "Son of man, because Tyre has said concerning Jerusalem, 'Aha! The gateway of the peoples is broken; it has turned to me; I will be filled, she that is laid waste,'
verses.after: “Son of man, Tyre said about Jerusalem, ‘Aha! The gateway of the peoples is broken! It has turned toward me. Now that she is ruined, I will be filled.’
verses.tsw_comparator: "Son of man, because Tyre has said concerning Jerusalem, 'Aha! The gateway of the peoples is broken; it has turned to me; I shall be filled, she that is laid waste,'

verses.rationale: Retains the sea comparison introducing the city's fall.
verses.before: so thus says the LORD GOD: Look, I am against you, O Tyre, and I will bring up many nations against you, as the sea causes its waves to come up.
verses.after: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I am against you, Tyre. I will bring many nations up against you, as the sea brings up its waves.
verses.tsw_comparator: therefore thus says the LORD GOD: Behold, I am against you, O Tyre, and I will bring up many nations against you, as the sea causes its waves to come up.

verses.rationale: Preserves they-to-I change and scraped-rock image.
verses.before: They will destroy the walls of Tyre and break down her towers; I will also scrape her debris from her and make her a bare rock.
verses.after: They will destroy Tyre’s walls and tear down her towers. I will scrape away her soil and make her a bare rock.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will destroy the walls of Tyre and break down her towers; I will also scrape her debris from her and make her a bare rock.

verses.rationale: Keeps nets, sea and plunder together.
verses.before: She will be a place for spreading nets among the sea, for I have spoken, declares the LORD GOD, and she will become spoil for the nations.
verses.after: She will be a place for spreading nets out in the sea, for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD. She will become plunder for the nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: She will be a place for spreading nets in the midst of the sea, for I have spoken, declares the LORD GOD, and she shall become spoil for the nations.

verses.rationale: Clarifies daughter settlements while retaining violent personification.
verses.before: Also her daughters who are in the field will be slain by the sword, and they will know that I am the LORD."
verses.after: Her daughter towns on the mainland will be killed by the sword. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Also her daughters who are in the field will be slain by the sword, and they will know that I am the LORD."

verses.rationale: Preserves royal title and northern approach.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD GOD: "Look, I will bring against Tyre Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the north, king of kings, with horses and chariots, with horsemen and a vast company and many people.
verses.after: “For this is what the Lord GOD says: I am bringing Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon against Tyre from the north, a king of kings, with horses, chariots, cavalry, and a great mass of troops.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD GOD: "Behold, I will bring against Tyre Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the north, king of kings, with horses and chariots, with horsemen and a vast company and many people.

verses.rationale: Keeps three siege actions and singular attacker.
verses.before: He will slay your daughters on the field with the sword, and he will set siege works against you, build a ramp against you, and raise a protective shield against you.
verses.after: He will kill your daughter towns on the mainland by the sword. He will build siegeworks against you, heap up a ramp, and raise a shield against you.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will slay your daughters on the field with the sword, and he will set siege works against you, build a ramp against you, and raise a protective shield against you.

verses.rationale: Renders rare siege term provisionally in context.
verses.before: He will direct the thrust of battering rams against your walls, and with his weapons he will break down your towers.
verses.after: He will direct the blows of his battering ram against your walls and tear down your towers with his weapons.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will direct the thrust of battering rams against your walls, and with his weapons he will break down your towers.

verses.rationale: Keeps dust, sound and breach comparison.
verses.before: From the abundance of his horses, their dust will cover you; your walls will shake at the noise of the cavalry, wagons, and chariots, when he enters your gates as men enter a breached city.
verses.after: His many horses will cover you with dust. Your walls will shake at the sound of cavalry, wheels, and chariots as he enters your gates, as men enter a breached city.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the abundance of his horses, their dust will cover you; your walls will shake at the noise of the cavalry, wagons, and chariots, when he enters your gates as men enter a breached city.

verses.rationale: Retains pillars without specifying an unmentioned cult.
verses.before: With the hooves of his horses he will trample all your streets; he will kill your people with the sword, and your mighty pillars will fall to the ground.
verses.after: His horses’ hooves will trample all your streets. He will kill your people by the sword, and your mighty pillars will fall to the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: With the hooves of his horses he will trample all your streets; he will kill your people with the sword, and your mighty pillars will fall to the ground.

verses.rationale: Preserves shift to plural attackers and material list.
verses.before: They will plunder your riches and seize your merchandise; they will break down your walls and destroy your pleasant houses; your stones, wood, and debris they will throw into the water.
verses.after: They will plunder your wealth and loot your goods. They will tear down your walls and demolish your fine houses, throwing your stones, timber, and soil into the water.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will plunder your riches and seize your merchandise; they will break down your walls and destroy your pleasant houses; your stones, wood, and debris they will throw into the water.

verses.rationale: Keeps two distinct forms of silenced music.
verses.before: I will cause the noise of your songs to cease, and the sound of your harps will no longer be heard.
verses.after: I will silence the sound of your songs; the music of your lyres will be heard no more.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will cause the noise of your songs to cease, and the sound of your harps will no longer be heard.

verses.rationale: Does not qualify the absolute rebuilding statement.
verses.before: I will make you a bare rock; you will be a place for spreading nets. You will never be rebuilt, for I, the LORD, have spoken, declares the LORD GOD.
verses.after: I will make you a bare rock, a place for spreading nets. You will never be rebuilt, for I, the LORD, have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will make you a bare rock; you will be a place for spreading nets. You will never be rebuilt, for I, the LORD, have spoken, declares the LORD GOD.

verses.rationale: Retains rhetorical question and suffering sounds.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD GOD to Tyre: Will not the coastlands tremble at the sound of your downfall, when the wounded groan, and the massacre occurs in your midst?
verses.after: “This is what the Lord GOD says to Tyre: Will the coastlands not shake at the sound of your fall, as the wounded groan and slaughter takes place within you?
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD GOD to Tyre: Shall not the coastlands tremble at the sound of your downfall, when the wounded groan, and the massacre occurs in your midst?

verses.rationale: Preserves clothing metaphor and repeated trembling.
verses.before: Then all the princes of the sea will step down from their thrones, lay aside their robes, and strip off their embroidered garments. They will put on trembling; they will sit on the ground, tremble every moment, and be appalled at you.
verses.after: All the princes of the sea will step down from their thrones, remove their robes, and strip off their embroidered clothes. Clothed in trembling, they will sit on the ground, trembling every moment, appalled at you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all the princes of the sea will step down from their thrones, lay aside their robes, and strip off their embroidered garments. They will put on trembling; they will sit on the ground, tremble every moment, and be appalled at you.

verses.rationale: Keeps difficult sea-origin wording and personified lament.
verses.before: They will take up a lamentation for you and say to you, 'How you have perished, inhabited from the seas, O city renowned, who was strong on the sea, she and her inhabitants, who caused their terror to be on all her inhabitants!
verses.after: They will take up a lament over you and say: ‘How you have perished, you who were settled from the seas, the celebrated city, mighty on the sea— you and your inhabitants, who spread terror to all who lived there!’
verses.tsw_comparator: They will take up a lamentation for you and say to you, 'How you have perished, inhabited from the seas, O city renowned, who was strong on the sea, she and her inhabitants, who caused their terror to be on all her inhabitants!

verses.rationale: Preserves parallel coastland imagery and departure.
verses.before: Now the coastlands will tremble on the day of your fall; yes, the coastlands that are in the sea will be alarmed at your departure.'"
verses.after: ‘Now the coastlands tremble on the day you fall; the islands in the sea are dismayed at your passing.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the coastlands will tremble on the day of your fall; yes, the coastlands that are in the sea will be alarmed at your departure.'"

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated when clauses leading into descent.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD GOD: "When I make you a desolated city, like cities that are not inhabited, when I bring up the deep over you and the great waters cover you,
verses.after: “For this is what the Lord GOD says: When I make you a ruined city, like cities no one inhabits, when I bring the deep up over you and the great waters cover you,
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD GOD: "When I make you a desolated city, like cities that are not inhabited, when I bring up the deep over you and the great waters cover you,

verses.rationale: Retains pinned positive final clause rather than emending it.
verses.before: then I will bring you down with people who go down to the pit, to the people of old, and I will make you dwell in the lower parts of the earth, like the ancient ruins, with people who go down to the pit, so you will not be inhabited; but I will set glory in the land of the living.
verses.after: I will bring you down with those who descend to the pit, to the people of long ago. I will settle you in the world below, among ancient ruins, with those who descend to the pit, so you will not be inhabited. But I will set splendor in the land of the living.
verses.tsw_comparator: then I will bring you down with those who go down to the pit, to the people of old, and I will make you dwell in the lower parts of the earth, like the ancient ruins, with those who go down to the pit, so you will not be inhabited; but I will set glory in the land of the living.

verses.rationale: Retains permanent absence without historical harmonization.
verses.before: I will make you a terror, and you will be no more; you will be sought, but you will never be found again, declares the LORD GOD."
verses.after: I will make you a terror, and you will be no more. People will search for you, but you will never again be found, declares the Lord GOD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will make you a terror, and you shall be no more; you will be sought, but you will never be found again, declares the LORD GOD."

verses.rationale: Keeps the recurring introduction concise.
verses.before: It came about that the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: It came about that the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

verses.rationale: Identifies genre before the ship portrait.
verses.before: "Now, you, son of man, lift up a lamentation over Tyre.
verses.after: “Son of man, take up a lament over Tyre.
verses.tsw_comparator: "Now, you, son of man, lift up a lamentation over Tyre.

verses.rationale: Follows read-form dwelling and retains Tyre's boast.
verses.before: Say to Tyre, who dwells at the entrances of the sea, who trades with the peoples in many coastlands, 'Thus says the LORD GOD: Tyre, you have said, "I am perfect in beauty."
verses.after: Say to Tyre, who sits at the entrances to the sea, trading with peoples on many coastlands: This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Tyre, you said, “I am perfect in beauty.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Say to Tyre, who dwells at the entrances of the sea, who trades with the peoples in many coastlands, 'Thus says the LORD GOD: Tyre, you have said, "I am perfect in beauty."

verses.rationale: Keeps heart-of-seas and beauty repetition.
verses.before: In the heart of the seas are your borders. Your builders have perfected your beauty.
verses.after: Your borders lie in the heart of the seas; your builders perfected your beauty.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the heart of the seas are your borders. Your builders have perfected your beauty.

verses.rationale: Retains timber origins and distinct ship parts.
verses.before: They made all your planks of cypress from Senir. They took a cedar from Lebanon to make a mast for you.
verses.after: They made all your planks from junipers of Senir; they took a cedar from Lebanon to make your mast.
verses.tsw_comparator: They made all your planks of cypress from Senir. They took a cedar from Lebanon to make a mast for you.

verses.rationale: Uses provisional timber reading with uncertainty noted.
verses.before: They made your oars of oaks from Bashan. They made your deck of inlaid ivory from the coasts of Kittim.
verses.after: They made your oars from oaks of Bashan, your deck of cypress from the coastlands of Kittim, inlaid with ivory.
verses.tsw_comparator: They made your oars of oaks from Bashan. They made your deck of inlaid ivory from the coasts of Kittim.

verses.rationale: Keeps sail/banner relation and colored canopy.
verses.before: Fine embroidered linen from Egypt was your sail, serving as your banner; blue and purple from the coasts of Elishah covered you.
verses.after: Embroidered linen from Egypt was your sail and served as your banner. Blue and purple cloth from Elishah’s coastlands was your awning.
verses.tsw_comparator: Fine embroidered linen from Egypt was your sail, serving as your banner; blue and purple from the coasts of Elishah covered you.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes rowers from Tyrian pilots.
verses.before: Inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad were your rowers; your skilled men, O Tyre, were among you; they were your pilots.
verses.after: People of Sidon and Arvad were your rowers; your own skilled men, Tyre, were aboard as pilots.
verses.tsw_comparator: Inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad were your rowers; your skilled men, O Tyre, were among you; they were your pilots.

verses.rationale: Retains elders and shifts ship image into commerce.
verses.before: The elders of Gebal and its skilled men were in you, caulking your seams. All the ships of the sea with their sailors were among you to carry your merchandise.
verses.after: Elders of Gebal and its skilled men were aboard to repair your seams. All the ships of the sea and their sailors came to you to exchange your goods.
verses.tsw_comparator: The elders of Gebal and its skilled men were in you, caulking your seams. All the ships of the sea with their sailors were among you to carry your merchandise.

verses.rationale: Preserves all three peoples and martial display.
verses.before: Persia, Lud, and Put were in your army; they hung shield and helmet in you; they gave you your splendor.
verses.after: Men of Persia, Lud, and Put served in your army as your warriors. They hung shield and helmet on you and gave you splendor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Persia, Lud, and Put were in your army; they hung shield and helmet in you; they gave you your splendor.

verses.rationale: Retains uncertain Gammadim name and recurring beauty.
verses.before: The sons of Arvad and your army were on your walls all around, and the Gammadites were in your towers. They hung their shields on your walls all around; they perfected your beauty.
verses.after: Men of Arvad and your army stood on your walls all around; the Gammadim were in your towers. They hung their shields all around your walls and perfected your beauty.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of Arvad and your army were on your walls all around, and the Gammadites were in your towers. They hung their shields on your walls all around; they perfected your beauty.

verses.rationale: Keeps four metals and direction of exchange.
verses.before: Tarshish traded with you because of your great wealth of all kinds; silver, iron, tin, and lead they exchanged for your merchandise.
verses.after: “‘Tarshish traded with you because of your abundant wealth. They paid for your wares with silver, iron, tin, and lead.
verses.tsw_comparator: Tarshish traded with you because of your great wealth of all kinds; silver, iron, tin, and lead they exchanged for your merchandise.

verses.rationale: Makes human trade explicit without euphemism.
verses.before: Javan, Tubal, and Meshech were your merchants, exchanging human beings and vessels of bronze for your merchandise.
verses.after: Javan, Tubal, and Meshech were your traders. They exchanged human lives and bronze vessels for your goods.
verses.tsw_comparator: Javan, Tubal, and Meshech were your merchants, exchanging human beings and vessels of bronze for your merchandise.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes three traded animal categories.
verses.before: From the house of Togarmah they gave you horses, war horses, and mules for your wares.
verses.after: From Beth-togarmah they brought horses, warhorses, and mules in exchange for your wares.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the house of Togarmah they gave you horses, war horses, and mules for your wares.

verses.rationale: Retains pinned Dedan rather than substituting Rhodes.
verses.before: The men of Dedan were your traders; many coastlands were your own agents; ivory and ebony they brought as your payment.
verses.after: The people of Dedan traded with you. Many coastlands were your customers; they paid you in ivory tusks and ebony.
verses.tsw_comparator: The men of Dedan were your traders; many coastlands were your own agents; ivory and ebony they brought as your payment.

verses.rationale: Keeps Aram and six commodities; stones provisional.
verses.before: Aram traded with you due to the abundance of your goods; with emeralds, purple, embroidered work, fine linen, coral, and rubies they exchanged for your wares.
verses.after: Aram traded with you because of your many products. They paid for your wares with turquoise, purple cloth, embroidery, fine linen, coral, and rubies.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aram traded with you due to the abundance of your goods; with emeralds, purple, embroidered work, fine linen, coral, and rubies they exchanged for your wares.

verses.rationale: Retains unidentified pannag rather than inventing a product.
verses.before: Judah and the land of Israel were your traders; they exchanged wheat from Minnith, confections, honey, oil, and resin for your merchandise.
verses.after: Judah and the land of Israel traded with you. They exchanged wheat from Minnith, pannag, honey, oil, and balm for your goods.
verses.tsw_comparator: Judah and the land of Israel were your traders; they exchanged wheat from Minnith, confections, honey, oil, and resin for your merchandise.

verses.rationale: Keeps Helbon and provisional wool description.
verses.before: Damascus traded with you because of the abundance of your goods and all your wealth, with wine from Helbon and white wool.
verses.after: Damascus traded with you for your many products and abundant wealth, bringing wine from Helbon and white wool.
verses.tsw_comparator: Damascus traded with you because of the abundance of your goods and all your wealth, with wine from Helbon and white wool.

verses.rationale: Preserves difficult names with note rather than conflation.
verses.before: Vedan and Javan from Uzal exchanged wrought iron, cassia, and calamus for your merchandise.
verses.after: Vedan and Javan from Uzal paid for your wares. Wrought iron, cassia, and aromatic cane were among your traded goods.
verses.tsw_comparator: Vedan and Javan from Uzal exchanged wrought iron, cassia, and calamus for your merchandise.

verses.rationale: Renders riding textiles naturally without extra detail.
verses.before: Dedan was your merchant in saddlecloths for riding.
verses.after: Dedan traded saddlecloths with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Dedan was your merchant in saddlecloths for riding.

verses.rationale: Keeps rulers and all three livestock terms.
verses.before: Arabia and all the princes of Kedar were agents doing business with you in lambs, rams, and goats.
verses.after: Arabia and all the princes of Kedar were your customers. They traded with you in lambs, rams, and male goats.
verses.tsw_comparator: Arabia and all the princes of Kedar were agents doing business with you in lambs, rams, and goats.

verses.rationale: Preserves paired traders and quality emphasis.
verses.before: The traders of Sheba and Raamah were your merchants; they traded in all kinds of spices, stones of value, and gold for your goods.
verses.after: The traders of Sheba and Raamah traded with you. They paid for your wares with the finest spices, all kinds of precious stones, and gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: The traders of Sheba and Raamah were your merchants; they traded in all kinds of spices, stones of value, and gold for your goods.

verses.rationale: Keeps the full place-name list.
verses.before: Haran, Canneh, and Eden, the traders of Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad traded with you.
verses.after: Haran, Canneh, Eden, the traders of Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad traded with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Haran, Canneh, and Eden, the traders of Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad traded with you.

verses.rationale: Uses textile reading provisionally; alternatives in note.
verses.before: These were your merchants in splendid apparel, in clothes of blue and embroidered work, in cords, firmly twisted, and secured in your market.
verses.after: They traded with you in splendid clothes, blue and embroidered wraps, and multicolored rugs bound and secured with cords.
verses.tsw_comparator: These were your merchants in splendid apparel, in clothes of blue and embroidered work, in cords, firmly twisted, and secured in your market.

verses.rationale: Carries the trade inventory back into ship poetry.
verses.before: The ships of Tarshish were your carriers for your merchandise; you were filled and heavily laden in the heart of the seas.
verses.after: Ships of Tarshish carried your merchandise. You were filled and heavily laden in the heart of the seas.
verses.tsw_comparator: The ships of Tarshish were your carriers for your merchandise; you were filled and heavily laden in the heart of the seas.

verses.rationale: Retains location refrain and wind direction.
verses.before: Your rowers have brought you into great waters; the east wind has shattered you in the heart of the seas.
verses.after: Your rowers took you into great waters, but the east wind shattered you in the heart of the seas.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your rowers have brought you into great waters; the east wind has shattered you in the heart of the seas.

verses.rationale: Preserves the complete accumulating loss inventory.
verses.before: Your wealth, your wares, your merchandise, your mariners, your pilots, those repairing your seams, and all your warriors who are in you, along with all your company in your midst, will fall into the heart of the seas on the day of your downfall.
verses.after: Your wealth, wares, and goods, your sailors and pilots, those who repaired your seams and traded your goods, all your warriors aboard and the whole company within you— they will fall into the heart of the seas on the day of your fall.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your wealth, your wares, your merchandise, your mariners, your pilots, those repairing your seams, and all your warriors who are in you, along with all your company in your midst, will fall into the heart of the seas on the day of your downfall.

verses.rationale: Keeps pilots' cry and uncertain land term noted.
verses.before: At the sound of the cry of your pilots, the countryside will shake.
verses.after: At the sound of your pilots’ cry, the shorelands will shake.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the sound of the cry of your pilots, the countryside will shake.

verses.rationale: Preserves all three seafaring groups.
verses.before: Everyone who handle the oar, the mariners, all the pilots of the sea, will come down from their ships; they will stand on the land,
verses.after: All who handle an oar will leave their ships. Sailors and all the sea’s pilots will stand on land.
verses.tsw_comparator: All who handle the oar, the mariners, all the pilots of the sea, will come down from their ships; they will stand on the land,

verses.rationale: Retains physical mourning gestures.
verses.before: and they will make their voice heard over you and cry out bitterly. They will throw dust on their heads and wallow in ashes.
verses.after: They will raise their voices over you and cry out bitterly, throwing dust on their heads and rolling in ashes.
verses.tsw_comparator: and they will make their voice heard over you and cry out bitterly. They will throw dust on their heads and wallow in ashes.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated bitterness and bodily lament.
verses.before: They will make themselves bald for you and gird themselves with sackcloth; they will weep over you in bitterness of soul, with bitter mourning.
verses.after: They will shave their heads for you and wrap themselves in sackcloth. With bitter hearts they will weep over you, a bitter mourning.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will make themselves bald for you and gird themselves with sackcloth; they will weep over you in bitterness of soul, with bitter mourning.

verses.rationale: Reads difficult wailing phrase in lament context.
verses.before: In their wailing they will take up a lamentation for you and lament over you: "Who is like Tyre, silent and destroyed among the sea?"
verses.after: In their wailing they will take up a lament for you: “Who is like Tyre, now silenced in the midst of the sea?”
verses.tsw_comparator: In their wailing they will take up a lamentation for you and lament over you: "Who is like Tyre, silent and destroyed in the midst of the sea?"

verses.rationale: Keeps former international abundance before collapse.
verses.before: When your wares went out from the seas, you satisfied many peoples; you enriched the kings of the earth with your great wealth and merchandise.
verses.after: When your wares went out across the seas, you satisfied many peoples. Your great wealth and merchandise enriched the kings of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: When your wares went out from the seas, you satisfied many peoples; you enriched the kings of the earth with your great wealth and merchandise.

verses.rationale: Retains shift from wealth to total loss.
verses.before: Now you are shattered by the seas in the depths of the waters; your merchandise and all your company have fallen in your midst.
verses.after: Now you are shattered by the seas, in the depths of the waters; your merchandise and all your company have fallen with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now you are shattered by the seas in the depths of the waters; your merchandise and all your company have fallen in your midst.

verses.rationale: Preserves collective reaction and facial distress.
verses.before: All the inhabitants of the coastlands are appalled at you, and their kings shudder with horror, their faces are distorted.
verses.after: All who live on the coastlands are appalled at you. Their kings shudder with horror; their faces are troubled.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the inhabitants of the coastlands are appalled at you, and their kings shudder with horror, their faces are distorted.

verses.rationale: Retains hissing and final absolute refrain.
verses.before: The merchants among the peoples hiss at you; you have become a horror and will be no more forever.'"
verses.after: Merchants among the peoples hiss at you. You have become a terror, and you will be no more forever.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: The merchants among the peoples hiss at you; you have become a horror and shall be no more forever.'"

verses.rationale: Retains standard oracle introduction.
verses.before: The word of the LORD came to me:
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word of the LORD came to me:

verses.rationale: Keeps ruler's divine claim and human correction.
verses.before: “Son of man, say to the ruler of Tyre: Thus says the LORD GOD: Because your heart has become proud, and you have said, ‘I am a god; I sit in the seat of gods in the heart of the seas,’ though you are human and not a god, you have made your heart like the heart of a god.
verses.after: “Son of man, tell the ruler of Tyre: This is what the Lord GOD says: Your heart grew proud, and you said, ‘I am a god. I sit on a divine throne in the heart of the seas.’ Yet you are human, not a god, though you consider your mind equal to a god’s.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Son of man, say to the ruler of Tyre: Thus says the LORD GOD: Because your heart has become proud, and you have said, ‘I am a god; I sit in the seat of gods in the heart of the seas,’ though you are human and not a god, you have made your heart like the heart of a god.

verses.rationale: Keeps the taunt and read-form Daniel.
verses.before: Look, you are wiser than Daniel; no secret is hidden from you.
verses.after: So you are wiser than Daniel! No secret is hidden from you!
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, you are wiser than Daniel; no secret is hidden from you.

verses.rationale: Preserves wisdom-to-wealth causal sequence.
verses.before: By your wisdom and your understanding you have gained wealth for yourself and stored gold and silver in your treasuries.
verses.after: By your wisdom and understanding you acquired wealth, gathering gold and silver into your treasuries.
verses.tsw_comparator: By your wisdom and your understanding you have gained wealth for yourself and stored gold and silver in your treasuries.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated wealth and resulting pride.
verses.before: By your great wisdom in your trading you have increased your wealth, and your heart has become proud because of your wealth.
verses.after: Through your great skill in trading you increased your wealth, and your wealth made your heart proud.
verses.tsw_comparator: By your great wisdom in your trading you have increased your wealth, and your heart has become proud because of your wealth.

verses.rationale: Repeats the ruler's claimed divine mind.
verses.before: So thus says the LORD GOD: Because you have made your heart like the heart of a god,
verses.after: “Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Because you consider your mind equal to a god’s,
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus says the LORD GOD: Because you have made your heart like the heart of a god,

verses.rationale: Retains unusual beauty-of-wisdom image.
verses.before: so, look, I am bringing strangers against you, the most ruthless of nations. They will draw their swords against the beauty of your wisdom, and they will profane your splendor.
verses.after: I am bringing foreigners against you, the most ruthless of nations. They will draw their swords against the beauty of your wisdom and profane your splendor.
verses.tsw_comparator: therefore, look, I am bringing strangers against you, the most ruthless of nations. They will draw their swords against the beauty of your wisdom, and they will profane your splendor.

verses.rationale: Links pit and sea with actual death.
verses.before: They will bring you down to the pit, and you will die the deaths of the slain in the heart of the seas.
verses.after: They will bring you down to the pit. You will die the death of the slain in the heart of the seas.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will bring you down to the pit, and you will die the deaths of the slain in the heart of the seas.

verses.rationale: Keeps direct challenge and repeated human limitation.
verses.before: Will you still say, ‘I am a god,’ before the one who kills you? But you are human and not a god in the hand of people who wound you.
verses.after: Will you still say, ‘I am a god,’ before the one killing you? You are human, not a god, in the hands of those who wound you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Will you still say, ‘I am a god,’ before the one who kills you? But you are human and not a god in the hand of those who wound you.

verses.rationale: Preserves ancient circumcision distinction without expansion.
verses.before: You will die the deaths of the uncircumcised by the hand of strangers, for I have spoken, declares the LORD GOD.”
verses.after: You will die the death of the uncircumcised at the hands of foreigners, for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You will die the deaths of the uncircumcised by the hand of strangers, for I have spoken, declares the LORD GOD.”

verses.rationale: Separates the following lament from prior oracle.
verses.before: The word of the LORD came to me:
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word of the LORD came to me:

verses.rationale: Retains king as addressee and seal image.
verses.before: “Son of man, raise a lament over the king of Tyre, and say to him: Thus says the LORD GOD: You were the seal of perfection, full of wisdom and complete in beauty.
verses.after: “Son of man, take up a lament over the king of Tyre. Tell him: This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘You were the seal of perfection, full of wisdom and perfect in beauty.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Son of man, raise a lament over the king of Tyre, and say to him: Thus says the LORD GOD: You were the seal of perfection, full of wisdom and complete in beauty.

verses.rationale: Preserves nine stones; uncertain gem and craft terms noted.
verses.before: You were in Eden, the garden of God; every precious stone was your covering: ruby, topaz, and diamond; beryl, onyx, and jasper; sapphire, turquoise, and emerald; and gold. The workmanship of your tambourines and your settings was prepared in you on the day you were created.
verses.after: You were in Eden, the garden of God. Every precious stone covered you: carnelian, topaz, and diamond, beryl, onyx, and jasper, sapphire, turquoise, and emerald, with gold. Your settings and mountings were prepared on the day you were created.
verses.tsw_comparator: You were in Eden, the garden of God; every precious stone was your covering: ruby, topaz, and diamond; beryl, onyx, and jasper; sapphire, turquoise, and emerald; and gold. The workmanship of your tambourines and your settings was prepared in you on the day you were created.

verses.rationale: Follows pinned pointing with alternative relation noted.
verses.before: You were an anointed cherub who covered; I placed you on the holy mountain of God. You walked about among stones of fire.
verses.after: You were an anointed guardian cherub, and I placed you there. You were on God’s holy mountain, walking among stones of fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: You were an anointed cherub who covered; I placed you on the holy mountain of God. You walked about among stones of fire.

verses.rationale: Preserves temporal contrast without theological identification.
verses.before: You were blameless in your ways from the day you were created, until injustice was found in you.
verses.after: You were blameless in your ways from the day you were created until wrongdoing was found in you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You were blameless in your ways from the day you were created, until injustice was found in you.

verses.rationale: Keeps trade, violence and divine expulsion connected.
verses.before: Through the abundance of your trade your midst was filled with violence, and you sinned. So I cast you out as profane from the mountain of God, and I destroyed you, covering cherub, from among the stones of fire.
verses.after: Through your abundant trade you were filled with violence, and you sinned. So I expelled you in disgrace from God’s mountain; I destroyed you, guardian cherub, from among the stones of fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: Through the abundance of your trade your midst was filled with violence, and you sinned. So I cast you out as profane from the mountain of God, and I destroyed you, covering cherub, from among the stones of fire.

verses.rationale: Retains wisdom corrupted by visible splendor.
verses.before: Your heart became proud because of your beauty; you corrupted your wisdom because of your splendor. I threw you to the earth; I set you before kings for them to gaze at you.
verses.after: Your beauty made your heart proud; you ruined your wisdom for the sake of your splendor. I threw you to the ground and set you before kings to stare at you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your heart became proud because of your beauty; you corrupted your wisdom because of your splendor. I threw you to the earth; I set you before kings for them to gaze at you.

verses.rationale: Preserves plural sanctuaries and internal fire.
verses.before: By the abundance of your iniquities, by the injustice of your trade, you profaned your sanctuaries. So I brought out fire from your midst; it consumed you. I made you ashes upon the earth before the eyes of everyone who saw you.
verses.after: By your many wrongs and dishonest trade you profaned your sanctuaries. So I brought fire out from within you, and it consumed you. I turned you to ashes on the ground in the sight of everyone watching.
verses.tsw_comparator: By the abundance of your iniquities, by the injustice of your trade, you profaned your sanctuaries. So I brought out fire from your midst; it consumed you. I made you ashes upon the earth before the eyes of all who saw you.

verses.rationale: Keeps refrain shared with Tyre's ship lament.
verses.before: Everyone who knew you among the peoples are appalled at you. You have become a horror, and you will be no more forever.”
verses.after: All who know you among the peoples are appalled at you. You have become a terror, and you will be no more forever.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: All who knew you among the peoples are appalled at you. You have become a horror, and you will be no more forever.”

verses.rationale: Marks a new oracle distinctly.
verses.before: The word of the LORD came to me:
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word of the LORD came to me:

verses.rationale: Names new target and embodied direction.
verses.before: “Son of man, set your face toward Sidon, and prophesy against her.
verses.after: “Son of man, turn your face toward Sidon and prophesy against her.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Son of man, set your face toward Sidon, and prophesy against her.

verses.rationale: Preserves second-to-third-person shift and divine holiness.
verses.before: Say: Thus says the LORD GOD: Look, I am against you, Sidon, and I will be glorified in your midst. They will know that I am the LORD when I execute judgments in her and show myself holy through her.
verses.after: Say: This is what the Lord GOD says: I am against you, Sidon. I will display my glory within you. They will know that I am the LORD when I carry out judgments in her and show myself holy within her.
verses.tsw_comparator: Say: Thus says the LORD GOD: Look, I am against you, Sidon, and I will be glorified in your midst. They will know that I am the LORD when I execute judgments in her and show myself holy through her.

verses.rationale: Keeps pestilence and surrounding sword distinct.
verses.before: For I will send plague into her, and blood into her streets. The slain will fall in her midst, as the sword comes against her from every side. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
verses.after: I will send pestilence into her and blood into her streets. The slain will fall within her as the sword strikes from every side. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I will send plague into her, and blood into her streets. The slain will fall in her midst, as the sword comes against her from every side. Then they will know that I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains plant images and despising neighbors.
verses.before: There will no longer be for the house of Israel a malignant briar or a painful thorn from all those around them who despise them. Then they will know that I am the LORD GOD.
verses.after: “The house of Israel will no longer have a pricking brier or a painful thorn among all the neighbors who despise them. Then they will know that I am the Lord GOD.
verses.tsw_comparator: There will no longer be for the house of Israel a malignant briar or a painful thorn from all those around them who despise them. Then they will know that I am the LORD GOD.

verses.rationale: Connects gathering, holiness and Jacob's land.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD GOD: When I gather the house of Israel from the peoples among whom they have been scattered, and show myself holy through them before the eyes of the nations, then they will live on their land, which I gave to my servant Jacob.
verses.after: “This is what the Lord GOD says: When I gather the house of Israel from the peoples among whom they were scattered, I will show myself holy through them in the sight of the nations. They will live on their own soil, which I gave to my servant Jacob.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD GOD: When I gather the house of Israel from the peoples among whom they have been scattered, and show myself holy through them before the eyes of the nations, then they will live on their land, which I gave to my servant Jacob.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated security rather than compressing it.
verses.before: They will live there securely. They will build houses and plant vineyards; they will live securely when I execute judgments on all around them who despise them. Then they will know that I am the LORD their God.”
verses.after: They will live there securely, building houses and planting vineyards. They will live securely when I carry out judgments against all their neighbors who despise them. Then they will know that I am the LORD their God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They will live there securely. They will build houses and plant vineyards; they will live securely when I execute judgments on all around them who despise them. Then they will know that I am the LORD their God.”

verses.rationale: Preserves all three date components.
verses.before: In the tenth year, in the tenth month, on the twelfth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying:
verses.after: In the tenth year, on the twelfth day of the tenth month, the word of the LORD came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: In the tenth year, in the tenth month, on the twelfth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying:

verses.rationale: Keeps ruler and nation as separate targets.
verses.before: "Son of man, set your face against Pharaoh king of Egypt and prophesy against him and against all Egypt.
verses.after: “Son of man, turn your face toward Pharaoh king of Egypt. Prophesy against him and against all Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: "Son of man, set your face against Pharaoh king of Egypt and prophesy against him and against all Egypt.

verses.rationale: Retains monster image and disputed creation boast with note.
verses.before: Speak and say: Thus says the LORD GOD: Look, I am against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great dragon lying among his rivers, who has said, 'My river is mine, and I have made it for myself.'
verses.after: Say: This is what the Lord GOD says: I am against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great monster lying among his Nile channels, who says, ‘My Nile is mine; I made it for myself.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Speak and say: Thus says the LORD GOD: Behold, I am against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great dragon lying in the midst of his rivers, who has said, 'My river is mine, and I have made it for myself.'

verses.rationale: Keeps fish-and-scales repetition and read-form hooks.
verses.before: I will put hooks in your jaws, and I will make the fish of your rivers cling to your scales. I will bring you up out of the midst of your rivers, and all the fish of your rivers will cling to your scales.
verses.after: I will put hooks in your jaws and make the fish of your channels cling to your scales. I will pull you up from your channels, with all their fish clinging to your scales.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will put hooks in your jaws, and I will make the fish of your rivers cling to your scales. I will bring you up out of the midst of your rivers, and all the fish of your rivers will cling to your scales.

verses.rationale: Retains unburied disposal and both scavenger groups.
verses.before: I will leave you in the wilderness, you and all the fish of your rivers. You will fall on the open field; you will not be gathered or buried. I have given you as food to the beasts of the land and to the birds of the heavens.
verses.after: I will abandon you in the wilderness, you and all the fish of your channels. You will fall in the open country, neither gathered nor collected. I have given you as food to the beasts of the earth and the birds of the sky.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will leave you in the wilderness, you and all the fish of your rivers. You will fall on the open field; you will not be gathered or buried. I have given you as food to the beasts of the land and to the birds of the heavens.

verses.rationale: Connects recognition with unreliable-support image.
verses.before: All the inhabitants of Egypt will know that I am the LORD, because they have been a staff of reed to the house of Israel.
verses.after: Then everyone living in Egypt will know that I am the LORD. For you have been a reed staff to the house of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the inhabitants of Egypt will know that I am the LORD, because they have been a staff of reed to the house of Israel.

verses.rationale: Follows read-form hand; retains difficult upright-back clause.
verses.before: When they grasped you with the hand, you broke and tore all their shoulders; and when they leaned upon you, you broke and made all their loins to shake."
verses.after: When they grasped you in their hand, you splintered and tore every shoulder. When they leaned on you, you broke and forced every back upright.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they grasped you with the hand, you broke and tore all their shoulders; and when they leaned upon you, you broke and made all their loins to shake."

verses.rationale: Preserves both human and animal destruction.
verses.before: So thus says the LORD GOD: "Look, I will bring a sword against you, and I will cut off from you human and animal.
verses.after: “Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I am bringing a sword against you and will cut off humans and animals from you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus says the LORD GOD: "Behold, I will bring a sword against you, and I will cut off from you human and animal.

verses.rationale: Names Pharaoh to clarify the renewed quoted boast.
verses.before: The land of Egypt will become a desolation and a waste. Then they will know that I am the LORD, because you have said, 'The river is mine, and I have made it.'
verses.after: Egypt will become a desolate waste. Then they will know that I am the LORD. Because Pharaoh said, ‘The Nile is mine; I made it,’
verses.tsw_comparator: The land of Egypt will become a desolation and a waste. Then they will know that I am the LORD, because you have said, 'The river is mine, and I have made it.'

verses.rationale: Keeps named geographic extent and accumulated desolation.
verses.before: So look, I am against you and against your rivers, and I will make the land of Egypt an utter waste and desolation, from Migdol to Syene, as far as the border of Cush.
verses.after: I am against you and your Nile channels. I will make Egypt a ruined, desolate waste, from Migdol to Syene, as far as the border of Cush.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore behold, I am against you and against your rivers, and I will make the land of Egypt an utter waste and desolation, from Migdol to Syene, as far as the border of Cush.

verses.rationale: Preserves absolute wording and forty-year span.
verses.before: No foot of human will pass through it, nor foot of animal will pass through it; and it will not be inhabited for forty years.
verses.after: No human foot will pass through it, nor any animal’s foot. It will be uninhabited for forty years.
verses.tsw_comparator: No foot of human will pass through it, nor foot of animal will pass through it; and it will not be inhabited for forty years.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated desolation and scattering verbs.
verses.before: I will make the land of Egypt desolate among desolated countries, and her cities will be a desolation among wasted cities for forty years; and I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the countries."
verses.after: I will make Egypt desolate among desolate lands. Its cities will lie desolate among ruined cities for forty years. I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the lands.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will make the land of Egypt desolate among desolated countries, and her cities shall be a desolation among wasted cities for forty years; and I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the countries."

verses.rationale: Keeps explicit restoration after stated period.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD GOD: "At the end of forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the peoples among whom they were scattered.
verses.after: “For this is what the Lord GOD says: At the end of forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the peoples among whom they were scattered.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD GOD: "At the end of forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the peoples among whom they were scattered.

verses.rationale: Retains Pathros and limited restoration.
verses.before: I will restore the fortunes of Egypt and bring them back to the land of Pathros, the land of their origin, and there they will be a lowly kingdom.
verses.after: I will restore Egypt’s fortunes and bring them back to Pathros, the land of their origin. There they will be a lowly kingdom.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will restore the fortunes of Egypt and bring them back to the land of Pathros, the land of their origin, and there they will be a lowly kingdom.

verses.rationale: Keeps comparative lowliness and loss of dominion.
verses.before: It will be the lowest of the kingdoms; it will never again lift itself up above the nations. I will make them small so that they will never again rule over the nations.
verses.after: It will be the lowliest of kingdoms and will never again exalt itself over the nations. I will make them few, so they no longer rule the nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will be the lowest of the kingdoms; it will never again lift itself up above the nations. I will make them small so that they shall never again rule over the nations.

verses.rationale: Preserves guilt tied to reliance on Egypt.
verses.before: It will never again be a source of confidence for the house of Israel, bringing iniquity to remembrance when they turn to them, and they will know that I am the LORD GOD."
verses.after: Egypt will no longer be a source of confidence for the house of Israel, calling their guilt to mind when they turn to it. Then they will know that I am the Lord GOD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: It will never again be a source of confidence for the house of Israel, bringing iniquity to remembrance when they turn to them, and they will know that I am the LORD GOD."

verses.rationale: Keeps later oracle's date in its received position.
verses.before: In the twenty-seventh year, in the first month, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying:
