verses.tsw_comparator: In the twenty-seventh year, in the first month, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying:

verses.rationale: Preserves unsuccessful payment and bodily toil.
verses.before: "Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made his army labor hard against Tyre; every head was made bald and every shoulder rubbed bare. Yet he had no wages from Tyre to give to him or his army for the labor he had performed against it.
verses.after: “Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made his army labor hard against Tyre. Every head was rubbed bald and every shoulder rubbed raw, yet neither he nor his army received wages from Tyre for the work they did against her.
verses.tsw_comparator: "Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made his army labor hard against Tyre; every head was made bald and every shoulder rubbed bare. Yet he had no wages from Tyre to give to him or his army for the labor he had performed against it.

verses.rationale: Retains three plundering clauses and wage comparison.
verses.before: So thus says the LORD GOD: Look, I will give the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. He will carry off her wealth, take her spoil, and seize her plunder; it will be wages for his army.
verses.after: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I am giving Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. He will carry off its wealth, seize its spoil, and take its plunder as wages for his army.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus says the LORD GOD: Behold, I will give the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. He will carry off her wealth, take her spoil, and seize her plunder; it will be wages for his army.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine ownership of military labor.
verses.before: I have given him the land of Egypt as his payment for which he labored, because they worked for me, declares the LORD GOD.
verses.after: I have given him Egypt as payment for the work he did, because they worked for me, declares the Lord GOD.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have given him the land of Egypt as his payment for which he labored, because they worked for me, declares the LORD GOD.

verses.rationale: Keeps horn and opened-mouth images with vocabulary support.
verses.before: On that day I will cause a horn to sprout for the house of Israel, and I will give you the opening of the mouth among them. Then they will know that I am the LORD."
verses.after: “On that day I will make a horn sprout for the house of Israel. I will give you an open mouth among them. Then they will know that I am the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day I will cause a horn to sprout for the house of Israel, and I will give you the opening of the mouth among them. Then they will know that I am the LORD."

verses.rationale: Retains recurring oracle introduction.
verses.before: The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves commanded lament and direct cry.
verses.before: "Son of man, prophesy and say: 'Thus says the LORD GOD: Wail, "Alas for the day!"
verses.after: “Son of man, prophesy. Say: This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Wail, “Alas for the day!”
verses.tsw_comparator: "Son of man, prophesy and say: 'Thus says the LORD GOD: Wail, "Alas for the day!"

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated nearness and cloud image.
verses.before: For the day is near, the day of the LORD is near— a day of clouds, a time of the nations.
verses.after: For a day is near, the day of the LORD is near— a day of clouds, a time for the nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the day is near, the day of the LORD is near— a day of clouds, a time of the nations.

verses.rationale: Preserves impact on Cush alongside Egypt's ruin.
verses.before: A sword will come upon Egypt, and anguish will be in Cush, when the slain fall in Egypt, and they take away her wealth, and her foundations are torn down.
verses.after: A sword will come upon Egypt, and anguish will seize Cush when the slain fall in Egypt, its wealth is carried off, and its foundations are torn down.
verses.tsw_comparator: A sword will come upon Egypt, and anguish will be in Cush, when the slain fall in Egypt, and they take away her wealth, and her foundations are torn down.

verses.rationale: Retains Cub and difficult covenant-land designation.
verses.before: Cush, Put, Lud, all Arabia, Kub, and the people of the land allied with them, will fall by the sword.'
verses.after: Cush, Put, Lud, all the mixed peoples, Cub, and the people of the covenant land will fall with them by the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: Cush, Put, Lud, all Arabia, Kub, and the people of the land allied with them, will fall by the sword.'

verses.rationale: Keeps full geographic repetition and both titles.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: People who uphold Egypt will fall, and her pride, her power will come down; from Migdol to Syene, they will fall within her by the sword— declares the LORD GOD.
verses.after: “‘This is what the LORD says: Egypt’s supporters will fall, and the pride of its strength will sink. From Migdol to Syene they will fall within it by the sword, declares the Lord GOD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: Those who uphold Egypt will fall, and her pride, her power will come down; from Migdol to Syene, they will fall within her by the sword— declares the LORD GOD.

verses.rationale: Preserves repetition and pronoun shift.
verses.before: They will be desolate among desolate lands, and her cities will be among ruined cities.
verses.after: They will lie desolate among desolate lands, and its cities will stand among ruined cities.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will be desolate among desolate lands, and her cities will be among ruined cities.

verses.rationale: Keeps recognition attached to fire and allies' collapse.
verses.before: Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I set a fire in Egypt and break all her helpers.
verses.after: Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I set fire to Egypt and all its helpers are broken.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I set a fire in Egypt and break all her helpers.

verses.rationale: Retains ships, divine sending and final arrival cry.
verses.before: On that day messengers will go forth from me in ships to terrify the secure Cushites, and anguish will be on them on the day of Egypt. For look, it is coming!
verses.after: On that day messengers will go out from me in ships to terrify unsuspecting Cush. Anguish will seize them on Egypt’s day. Look, it is coming!
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day messengers will go forth from me in ships to terrify the secure Cushites, and anguish will be on them on the day of Egypt. For behold, it is coming!

verses.rationale: Keeps multitude distinct from wealth where context shifts.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD GOD: 'I will put an end to the multitude of Egypt by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
verses.after: “‘This is what the Lord GOD says: I will put an end to Egypt’s multitude through Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD GOD: 'I will put an end to the multitude of Egypt by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.

verses.rationale: Retains ruthless agent and mass killing.
verses.before: He and his people with him, the most ruthless of nations, will be brought in to destroy the land. They will draw their swords against Egypt and fill the land with the slain.
verses.after: He and his people, the most ruthless of nations, will be brought in to destroy the land. They will draw their swords against Egypt and fill the land with the slain.
verses.tsw_comparator: He and his people with him, the most ruthless of nations, will be brought in to destroy the land. They will draw their swords against Egypt and fill the land with the slain.

verses.rationale: Keeps sale metaphor and divine agency.
verses.before: I will dry up the streams of the Nile and sell the land into the hands of evil people. I will make the land desolate and all that is in it, by the hand of strangers. I, the LORD, have spoken!
verses.after: I will dry up the Nile channels and sell the land into the hands of evil men. Through foreigners I will lay waste the land and everything in it. I, the LORD, have spoken.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will dry up the streams of the Nile and sell the land into the hands of evil people. I will make the land desolate and all that is in it, by the hand of strangers. I, the LORD, have spoken!

verses.rationale: Preserves doubled idol terms and native ruler clause.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD GOD: 'I will destroy the idols and put an end to the images in Memphis. There will no longer be a prince from the land of Egypt, and I will put fear in the land of Egypt.
verses.after: “‘This is what the Lord GOD says: I will destroy the idols and put an end to the worthless gods of Memphis. There will no longer be a prince from Egypt, and I will spread fear through Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD GOD: 'I will destroy the idols and put an end to the images in Memphis. There will no longer be a prince from the land of Egypt, and I will put fear in the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Uses established English city names with Hebrew names noted.
verses.before: I will make Pathros desolate, set fire to Zoan, and execute judgments on Thebes.
verses.after: I will lay Pathros waste, set fire to Zoan, and carry out judgments in Thebes.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will make Pathros desolate, set fire to Zoan, and execute judgments on Thebes.

verses.rationale: Keeps distinct fortress and populated city.
verses.before: I will pour out my wrath on Pelusium, the stronghold of Egypt, and cut off the multitude of Thebes.
verses.after: I will pour out my fury on Pelusium, Egypt’s stronghold, and cut off the multitude of Thebes.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will pour out my wrath on Pelusium, the stronghold of Egypt, and cut off the multitude of Thebes.

verses.rationale: Retains difficult daytime-enemies clause without substitution.
verses.before: I will set fire to Egypt; Pelusium will writhe in anguish, Thebes will be broken through, and Memphis will face adversaries in daylight.
verses.after: I will set fire to Egypt. Pelusium will writhe in anguish; Thebes will be breached, and Memphis will face enemies in broad daylight.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will set fire to Egypt; Pelusium will writhe in anguish, Thebes will be broken through, and Memphis will face adversaries in daylight.

verses.rationale: Keeps gender-specific young men and feminine cities.
verses.before: The young men of On and of Pi-beseth will fall by the sword, and these cities will go into captivity.
verses.after: The young men of On and Pi-beseth will fall by the sword, and the cities will go into captivity.
verses.tsw_comparator: The young men of On and of Pi-beseth will fall by the sword, and these cities will go into captivity.

verses.rationale: Keeps darkness, yoke and daughter image.
verses.before: At Tehaphnehes the day will be dark, when I break there the yokes of Egypt, and her proud strength will come to an end in her. She will be covered by a cloud, and her daughters will go into captivity.
verses.after: At Tahpanhes daylight will darken when I break Egypt’s yoke bars there and put an end to its proud strength. A cloud will cover the city, and its daughters will go into captivity.
verses.tsw_comparator: At Tehaphnehes the day will be dark, when I break there the yokes of Egypt, and her proud strength will come to an end in her. She will be covered by a cloud, and her daughters will go into captivity.

verses.rationale: Retains concluding recognition formula.
verses.before: Thus I will execute judgments on Egypt, and they will know that I am the LORD.'
verses.after: I will carry out judgments against Egypt. Then they will know that I am the LORD.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus I will execute judgments on Egypt, and they will know that I am the LORD.'

verses.rationale: Preserves complete dated transition.
verses.before: In the eleventh year, in the first month, on the seventh day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
verses.after: In the eleventh year, on the seventh day of the first month, the word of the LORD came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: In the eleventh year, in the first month, on the seventh day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps extended injury-and-healing image.
verses.before: "Son of man, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt. It has not been bound up to heal or to have a bandage applied, to bind it up and make it strong to wield a sword.
verses.after: “Son of man, I have broken Pharaoh king of Egypt’s arm. It has not been bound up for healing or wrapped in a bandage to give it strength to grip a sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: "Son of man, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt. It has not been bound up to heal or to have a bandage applied, to bind it up and make it strong to wield a sword.

verses.rationale: Preserves distinction between two arms.
verses.before: So thus says the LORD GOD: 'Look, I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and will break his arms, both the strong arm and the one that was broken, and I will cause the sword to fall from his hand.
verses.after: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt. I will break both his arms, the strong one and the broken one, and make the sword fall from his hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus says the LORD GOD: 'Behold, I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and will break his arms, both the strong arm and the one that was broken, and I will cause the sword to fall from his hand.

verses.rationale: Retains doubled dispersal formula.
verses.before: I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the lands.
verses.after: I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the lands.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the lands.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine sword and groaning defeated ruler.
verses.before: I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon and put my sword in his hand; and I will break the arms of Pharaoh, and he will groan before him with the moaning of a mortally wounded man.
verses.after: I will strengthen the arms of Babylon’s king and put my sword in his hand. I will break Pharaoh’s arms, and he will groan before him like a mortally wounded man.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon and put my sword in his hand; and I will break the arms of Pharaoh, and he will groan before him with the moaning of a mortally wounded man.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated empowerment without compression.
verses.before: I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, but the arms of Pharaoh will fall. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I place my sword in the hand of the king of Babylon, and he stretches it out against the land of Egypt.
verses.after: I will strengthen the arms of Babylon’s king, while Pharaoh’s arms fall limp. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I put my sword into Babylon’s king’s hand and he stretches it out against Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, but the arms of Pharaoh will fall. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I place my sword in the hand of the king of Babylon, and he stretches it out against the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Preserves closing repeated dispersal and recognition.
verses.before: I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the lands. Then they will know that I am the LORD."
verses.after: I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the lands. Then they will know that I am the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the lands. Then they will know that I am the LORD."

verses.rationale: Preserves all date elements.
verses.before: In the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:
verses.after: In the eleventh year, on the first day of the third month, the word of the LORD came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: In the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:

verses.rationale: Keeps question leading into historical tree comparison.
verses.before: Human one, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his multitude: Whom do you resemble in your greatness?
verses.after: “Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and his multitude: Who can compare with you in greatness?
verses.tsw_comparator: Human one, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his multitude: Whom do you resemble in your greatness?

verses.rationale: Retains pinned Assyria rather than altering to cypress.
verses.before: Look: Assyria was a cedar in Lebanon, beautiful in its branches, a forest giving shade, high in stature; its top was among the thick boughs.
verses.after: Look at Assyria: a cedar in Lebanon, with beautiful branches, a shaded thicket, and towering height, its top among the clouds.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look: Assyria was a cedar in Lebanon, beautiful in its branches, a forest giving shade, high in stature; its top was among the thick boughs.

verses.rationale: Keeps deep as water provider and spreading channels.
verses.before: Waters made it grow; the Deep made it high. Its rivers flowed around its planting, and it sent out its channels to all the trees of the field.
verses.after: Water made it grow; the deep made it tall. Its rivers flowed around the planting, and it sent its channels to all the trees of the field.
verses.tsw_comparator: Waters made it grow; the Deep made it high. Its rivers flowed around its planting, and it sent out its channels to all the trees of the field.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated water explanation and branching.
verses.before: So it grew taller than all the trees of the field. Its boughs multiplied, and its branches grew long because of abundant waters as it spread them out.
verses.after: So it towered above all the trees of the field. Its boughs multiplied, its branches grew long, spreading out with abundant water.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore it grew taller than all the trees of the field. Its boughs multiplied, and its branches grew long because of abundant waters as it spread them out.

verses.rationale: Keeps birth, nesting and human shelter distinct.
verses.before: In its boughs all the birds of the heavens nested; under its branches all the animals of the field gave birth; and in its shade all the many nations lived.
verses.after: All the birds of the sky nested in its boughs; all the beasts of the field gave birth beneath its branches. All the great nations lived in its shade.
verses.tsw_comparator: In its boughs all the birds of the heavens nested; under its branches all the animals of the field gave birth; and in its shade all the many nations lived.

verses.rationale: Retains visible beauty grounded in water.
verses.before: It was beautiful in its greatness, in the length of its branches, for its root was by abundant waters.
verses.after: It was beautiful in its greatness and in the length of its branches, for its roots reached abundant water.
verses.tsw_comparator: It was beautiful in its greatness, in the length of its branches, for its root was by abundant waters.

verses.rationale: Preserves complete tree comparison and repeated garden.
verses.before: Cedars could not rival it in the garden of God; cypresses were not like its boughs, and plane trees were not like its branches. No tree in the garden of God resembled it in its beauty.
verses.after: Cedars in God’s garden could not rival it. Junipers could not match its boughs, nor plane trees its branches. No tree in God’s garden matched its beauty.
verses.tsw_comparator: Cedars could not rival it in the garden of God; cypresses were not like its boughs, and plane trees were not like its branches. No tree in the garden of God resembled it in its beauty.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine gift before pride and fall.
verses.before: I made it beautiful with its many branches, and all the trees of Eden envied it, which were in the garden of God.
verses.after: I made it beautiful with its many branches, and all the trees of Eden in God’s garden envied it.
verses.tsw_comparator: I made it beautiful with its many branches, and all the trees of Eden envied it, which were in the garden of God.

verses.rationale: Retains second-to-third-person change explicitly.
verses.before: So, thus says the LORD GOD: Because it grew high in stature and set its top among the thick boughs, and its heart was lifted up because of its height,
verses.after: “Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Because you grew so tall, and it lifted its top among the clouds, its heart proud of its height,
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, thus says the LORD GOD: Because it grew high in stature and set its top among the thick boughs, and its heart was lifted up because of its height,

verses.rationale: Preserves emphatic action and moral cause.
verses.before: I gave it into the hand of a mighty one of the nations. He will surely deal with it according to its wickedness. I have driven it out.
verses.after: I handed it over to a mighty ruler of nations, who would surely deal with it. I drove it out because of its wickedness.
verses.tsw_comparator: I gave it into the hand of a mighty one of the nations. He will surely deal with it according to its wickedness. I have driven it out.

verses.rationale: Keeps spatial spread and repeated abandonment.
verses.before: Foreigners cut it down, the ruthless ones of the nations, and left it. On the mountains and in all the valleys its branches fell; its boughs were broken in all the ravines of the land. All the peoples of the earth came down from its shade and left it.
verses.after: Foreigners, the most ruthless of nations, cut it down and abandoned it. Its branches fell on the mountains and in every valley; its boughs broke in all the ravines of the land. All the peoples of the earth left its shade and abandoned it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Foreigners cut it down, the ruthless ones of the nations, and left it. On the mountains and in all the valleys its branches fell; its boughs were broken in all the ravines of the land. All the peoples of the earth came down from its shade and left it.

verses.rationale: Reverses living-tree shelter into fallen-tree occupation.
verses.before: Upon its fallen trunk all the birds of the heavens settle, and among its branches are all the animals of the field,
verses.after: All the birds of the sky settle on its fallen trunk, and all the beasts of the field rest on its branches.
verses.tsw_comparator: Upon its fallen trunk all the birds of the heavens settle, and among its branches are all the animals of the field,

verses.rationale: Preserves tree-to-human movement and mortality conclusion.
verses.before: so that none of the trees by the waters may grow high in stature, or set their tops among the thick boughs, and none who drink water may stand tall in their height. For all of them are given over to death, to the land below, among mortals, with people who go down to the Pit.
verses.after: This happened so that no well-watered tree would exalt itself in height or lift its top among the clouds, and no water-drinking tree would stand proud in its height. For they are all given over to death, to the world below, among human beings who descend to the pit.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that none of the trees by the waters may grow high in stature, or set their tops among the thick boughs, and none who drink water may stand tall in their height. For all of them are given over to death, to the land below, among mortals, with those who go down to the Pit.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine mourning actions and water withdrawal.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD GOD: On the day it went down to Sheol, I caused mourning. I covered the Deep over it and held back its rivers, and abundant waters were restrained. Because of it I darkened Lebanon, and because of it all the trees of the field languished.
verses.after: “This is what the Lord GOD says: On the day it went down to Sheol, I caused mourning. I covered the deep for it, held back its rivers, and stopped the great waters. I darkened Lebanon over it, and all the trees of the field fainted because of it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD GOD: On the day it went down to Sheol, I caused mourning. I covered the Deep over it and held back its rivers, and abundant waters were restrained. Because of it I darkened Lebanon, and because of it all the trees of the field languished.

verses.rationale: Retains surprising consolation among the dead.
verses.before: At the sound of its fall I made nations tremble, when I brought it down to Sheol with people who go down to the Pit. Then in the land below all the trees of Eden were comforted— the choice and best trees of Lebanon, everyone who drink water.
verses.after: I made the nations shake at the sound of its fall, when I brought it down to Sheol with those who descend to the pit. Then all the trees of Eden, the choicest and best of Lebanon, all that drank water, were comforted in the world below.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the sound of its fall I made nations tremble, when I brought it down to Sheol with those who go down to the Pit. Then in the land below all the trees of Eden were comforted— the choice and best trees of Lebanon, all who drink water.

verses.rationale: Renders arm as supporting allies without naming them.
verses.before: They too went down with it to Sheol, to those slain by the sword— people who were its arm, who lived in its shade among the nations.
verses.after: They too went down with it to Sheol, to those slain by the sword—its allies who lived in its shade among the nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: They too went down with it to Sheol, to those slain by the sword— those who were its arm, who lived in its shade among the nations.

verses.rationale: Keeps final identification and humiliating burial company.
verses.before: Whom, then, do you resemble in glory and greatness among the trees of Eden? Yet you will be brought down with the trees of Eden to the land below. Among the uncircumcised you will lie with those slain by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his multitude, declares the LORD GOD.
verses.after: “Which tree of Eden compares with you in glory and greatness? Yet you will be brought down with the trees of Eden to the world below. You will lie among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his multitude, declares the Lord GOD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Whom, then, do you resemble in glory and greatness among the trees of Eden? Yet you will be brought down with the trees of Eden to the land below. Among the uncircumcised you will lie with those slain by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his multitude, declares the LORD GOD.

verses.rationale: Preserves complete date.
verses.before: In the twelfth year, in the twelfth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying:
verses.after: In the twelfth year, on the first day of the twelfth month, the word of the LORD came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: In the twelfth year, in the twelfth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying:

verses.rationale: Keeps lion/monster contrast and water disturbance.

verses.after: “Son of man, take up a lament over Pharaoh king of Egypt. Say to him: ‘You thought yourself a young lion among the nations, but you were a monster in the seas, thrashing in your rivers, muddying the water with your feet and fouling their streams.
verses.tsw_comparator: Mortal, raise a lament over Pharaoh king of Egypt, and say to him: > You compared yourself to a young lion among the nations, > yet you are like a sea monster in the seas. > You burst out in your rivers; > you muddied the waters with your feet > and fouled their rivers.

verses.rationale: Retains collective captors and divine net.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD GOD: > I will spread my net over you > in an assembly of many peoples, > and they will bring you up in my dragnet.
verses.after: This is what the Lord GOD says: I will spread my net over you with a great assembly of peoples, and they will haul you up in my dragnet.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD GOD: > I will spread my net over you > in an assembly of many peoples, > and they will bring you up in my dragnet.

verses.rationale: Keeps carcass disposal and comprehensive scavengers.
verses.before: I will cast you on the land; I will fling you out on the open field. I will cause every bird of the heavens to settle on you, and I will satisfy every wild creature of the earth with you.
verses.after: I will leave you on the land and fling you into the open country. I will settle every bird of the sky on you and feed the beasts of all the earth with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will cast you on the land; I will fling you out on the open field. I will cause every bird of the heavens to settle on you, and I will satisfy every wild creature of the earth with you.

verses.rationale: Retains vast body image; rare final noun provisional.
verses.before: I will put your flesh on the mountains and fill the valleys with your carcass.
verses.after: I will lay your flesh on the mountains and fill the valleys with your remains.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will put your flesh on the mountains and fill the valleys with your carcass.

verses.rationale: Preserves blood flooding rather than euphemizing it.
verses.before: I will drench the land, flowing from you, with your blood, as far as the mountains; and the ravines will be filled with you.
verses.after: I will drench the land with your flowing blood, as far as the mountains, and the ravines will be filled with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will drench the land, flowing from you, with your blood, as far as the mountains; and the ravines will be filled with you.

verses.rationale: Keeps extinction metaphor and distinct celestial lights.
verses.before: When I extinguish you, I will cover the heavens and darken their stars. I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon will not give its light.
verses.after: When I extinguish you, I will cover the heavens and darken their stars. I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon will not give its light.
verses.tsw_comparator: When I extinguish you, I will cover the heavens and darken their stars. I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon will not give its light.

verses.rationale: Preserves total darkness and oracle signature.
verses.before: All the lights of light in the heavens I will darken over you, and I will bring darkness upon your land, declares the LORD GOD.
verses.after: I will darken every shining light in the heavens over you and spread darkness over your land, declares the Lord GOD.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the lights of light in the heavens I will darken over you, and I will bring darkness upon your land, declares the LORD GOD.

verses.rationale: Retains downfall reaching unknown lands.
verses.before: I will trouble the hearts of many peoples when I bring news of your destruction among the nations, into lands you have not known.
verses.after: I will trouble the hearts of many peoples when I bring your downfall among the nations, to lands you have never known.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will trouble the hearts of many peoples when I bring news of your destruction among the nations, into lands you have not known.

verses.rationale: Keeps individual fear amid international reaction.
verses.before: I will make many peoples appalled at you, and their kings will shudder over you in horror when I brandish my sword before them. They will tremble continually, each for their own life, on the day of your downfall.
verses.after: I will make many peoples appalled at you. Their kings will shudder with horror when I brandish my sword before them. Each will tremble every moment for his own life on the day you fall.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will make many peoples appalled at you, and their kings will shudder over you in horror when I brandish my sword before them. They will tremble continually, each for their own life, on the day of your downfall.

verses.rationale: Names historical attacker within the lament.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD GOD: The sword of the king of Babylon will come against you.
verses.after: “‘For this is what the Lord GOD says: The sword of Babylon’s king will come against you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD GOD: The sword of the king of Babylon will come against you.

verses.rationale: Retains multitude repetition and total threat.
verses.before: By the swords of warriors I will cause your multitude to fall—all of them tyrants of nations. They will plunder the majesty of Egypt, and all its multitude will be destroyed.
verses.after: I will make your multitude fall by the swords of warriors, all of them the most ruthless of nations. They will destroy Egypt’s pride, and all its multitude will be wiped out.
verses.tsw_comparator: By the swords of warriors I will cause your multitude to fall—all of them tyrants of nations. They will plunder the majesty of Egypt, and all its multitude will be destroyed.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated muddying and nonhuman death.
verses.before: I will destroy all its livestock from beside abundant waters. No human foot will muddy them again, nor will the hooves of livestock muddy them.
verses.after: I will destroy all its livestock beside the great waters. No human foot will muddy them again, nor will an animal’s hoof muddy them.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will destroy all its livestock from beside abundant waters. No human foot will muddy them again, nor will the hooves of livestock muddy them.

verses.rationale: Keeps unsettling stillness and oil comparison.
verses.before: Then I will let their waters settle, and make their rivers flow like oil, declares the LORD GOD.
verses.after: Then I will let their waters settle and make their rivers flow like oil, declares the Lord GOD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I will let their waters settle, and make their rivers flow like oil, declares the LORD GOD.

verses.rationale: Preserves three when clauses leading to recognition.
verses.before: When I make the land of Egypt a desolation, when the land is stripped of all that fills it, when I strike down everyone who live in it, then they will know that I am the LORD.
verses.after: When I make Egypt desolate, when the land is stripped of all it held, when I strike all who live there, then they will know that I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: When I make the land of Egypt a desolation, when the land is stripped of all that fills it, when I strike down all who live in it, then they will know that I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps female lamenters and repeated singing.
verses.before: This is a lament, and they will chant it as a lament. The daughters of the nations will chant it; over Egypt and over all its multitude they will chant it as a lament, declares the LORD GOD.
verses.after: This is a lament to be sung. The daughters of the nations will sing it; over Egypt and all its multitude they will sing it, declares the Lord GOD.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: This is a lament, and they will chant it as a lament. The daughters of the nations will chant it; over Egypt and over all its multitude they will chant it as a lament, declares the LORD GOD.

verses.rationale: Does not supply an absent month number.
verses.before: In the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying:
verses.after: In the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: In the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying:

verses.rationale: Retains prophetic command and personified daughters.
verses.before: Mortal, wail over the multitude of Egypt, and bring it down— her and the daughters of mighty nations— to the depths of the earth, with people who go down to the pit.
verses.after: “Son of man, wail over Egypt’s multitude. Bring her down, her and the daughters of mighty nations, to the world below, with those who descend to the pit.
verses.tsw_comparator: Mortal, wail over the multitude of Egypt, and bring it down— her and the daughters of mighty nations— to the depths of the earth, with those who go down to the pit.

verses.rationale: Keeps taunting question and burial command.
verses.before: Whom do you surpass in beauty? Go down, and lie with the uncircumcised.
verses.after: ‘Whom do you surpass in beauty? Go down and lie with the uncircumcised!’
verses.tsw_comparator: Whom do you surpass in beauty? Go down, and lie with the uncircumcised.

verses.rationale: Preserves shifting subjects and plural multitudes.
verses.before: They will fall among those slain by the sword. A sword has been given; drag her away, with all her multitudes.
verses.after: They will fall among those slain by the sword. She is given over to the sword. Drag her away with all her multitudes!
verses.tsw_comparator: They will fall among those slain by the sword. A sword has been given; drag her away, with all her multitudes.

verses.rationale: Keeps underworld speech and repeated dishonor.
verses.before: The mighty warriors will speak to him from the midst of Sheol, with his helpers: “They have gone down; they lie still, the uncircumcised, slain by the sword.”
verses.after: From the midst of Sheol the mighty warriors will speak of him and his helpers: ‘They have come down; they lie there, uncircumcised, slain by the sword.’
verses.tsw_comparator: The mighty warriors will speak to him from the midst of Sheol, with his helpers: “They have gone down; they lie still, the uncircumcised, slain by the sword.”

verses.rationale: Retains collective and ruler pronoun shifts.
verses.before: There is Assyria, with all its assembly; its graves are all around it— all of them slain, fallen by the sword—
verses.after: “Assyria is there with all her company, their graves around him, all of them slain, fallen by the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is Assyria, with all its assembly; its graves are all around it— all of them slain, fallen by the sword—

verses.rationale: Keeps grave arrangement and former terror.
verses.before: whose graves were placed in the farthest recesses of the pit, and whose assembly is around its grave. All of them were slain, fallen by the sword, who spread terror in the land of the living.
verses.after: Her graves are set in the depths of the pit, her company around her grave. All of them were slain, fallen by the sword, they who spread terror in the land of the living.
verses.tsw_comparator: whose graves were placed in the farthest recesses of the pit, and whose assembly is around its grave. All of them were slain, fallen by the sword, who spread terror in the land of the living.

verses.rationale: Retains the full repeated descent pattern.
verses.before: There is Elam, with all its multitude, around its grave; all of them slain, fallen by the sword, who went down uncircumcised to the depths of the earth. They spread their terror in the land of the living, and they bear their disgrace with people who go down to the pit.
verses.after: “Elam is there with all her multitude around her grave. All of them were slain, fallen by the sword, gone down uncircumcised to the world below. They spread their terror in the land of the living, and they bear their disgrace with those who descend to the pit.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is Elam, with all its multitude, around its grave; all of them slain, fallen by the sword, who went down uncircumcised to the depths of the earth. They spread their terror in the land of the living, and they bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit.

verses.rationale: Preserves repetitions and bed-for-grave image.
verses.before: Among the slain they made a bed for her, with all her multitude; her graves are all around it. All of them are uncircumcised, slain by the sword, because they spread their terror in the land of the living. They bear their disgrace with people who go down to the pit; she is placed among the slain.
verses.after: They have made a bed for her among the slain, with all her multitude, her graves around it. All of them are uncircumcised, slain by the sword. Because they spread terror in the land of the living, they bear their disgrace with those who descend to the pit. They have been laid among the slain.
verses.tsw_comparator: Among the slain they made a bed for her, with all her multitude; her graves are all around it. All of them are uncircumcised, slain by the sword, because they spread their terror in the land of the living. They bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit; she is placed among the slain.

verses.rationale: Keeps paired peoples and cause of humiliation.
verses.before: There are Meshech and Tubal, with all their multitude; their graves are all around them. All of them are uncircumcised, slain by the sword, because they spread their terror in the land of the living.
verses.after: “Meshech and Tubal are there with all their multitude, their graves around them. All of them are uncircumcised, pierced by the sword, because they spread their terror in the land of the living.
verses.tsw_comparator: There are Meshech and Tubal, with all their multitude; their graves are all around them. All of them are uncircumcised, slain by the sword, because they spread their terror in the land of the living.

verses.rationale: Retains pinned negative and guilt-on-bones difficulty.
verses.before: Yet they do not lie with the warriors fallen from among the uncircumcised, who went down to Sheol with their weapons of war, who placed their swords beneath their heads and whose guilt was upon their bones; for the terror of warriors was in the land of the living.
verses.after: They do not lie with the fallen warriors among the uncircumcised who went down to Sheol with their weapons of war, their swords laid beneath their heads, their guilt upon their bones, for the terror of the warriors was in the land of the living.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet they do not lie with the warriors fallen from among the uncircumcised, who went down to Sheol with their weapons of war, who placed their swords beneath their heads and whose guilt was upon their bones; for the terror of warriors was in the land of the living.

verses.rationale: Keeps direct address to condemned ruler.
verses.before: But you will be broken among the uncircumcised and lie with those slain by the sword.
verses.after: “You too will be broken among the uncircumcised and lie with those slain by the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you will be broken among the uncircumcised and lie with those slain by the sword.

verses.rationale: Preserves strength defeated and two burial companions.
verses.before: There is Edom, its kings and all its princes, who, despite their strength, are placed with those slain by the sword. They lie with the uncircumcised and with people who go down to the pit.
verses.after: “Edom is there, her kings and all her princes. Despite their might they were laid with those slain by the sword. They lie with the uncircumcised, with those who descend to the pit.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is Edom, its kings and all its princes, who, despite their strength, are placed with those slain by the sword. They lie with the uncircumcised and with those who go down to the pit.

verses.rationale: Retains Sidonians and strength-to-shame reversal.
verses.before: There are the princes of the north, all of them, and all the Sidonians, who have gone down with the slain. Ashamed despite the terror caused by their strength, they lie uncircumcised with those slain by the sword, and bear their disgrace with people who go down to the pit.
verses.after: “All the princes of the north are there, and all the Sidonians. They went down with the slain, ashamed despite the terror their strength inspired. They lie uncircumcised with those slain by the sword and bear their disgrace with those who descend to the pit.
verses.tsw_comparator: There are the princes of the north, all of them, and all the Sidonians, who have gone down with the slain. Ashamed despite the terror caused by their strength, they lie uncircumcised with those slain by the sword, and bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit.

verses.rationale: Keeps disturbing comfort rather than explaining it away.
verses.before: Pharaoh will see them and be comforted over all his multitude— Pharaoh and all his army, slain by the sword, declares the LORD GOD.
verses.after: “Pharaoh will see them and be comforted over all his multitude, Pharaoh and all his army slain by the sword, declares the Lord GOD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pharaoh will see them and be comforted over all his multitude— Pharaoh and all his army, slain by the sword, declares the LORD GOD.

verses.rationale: Follows read-form my terror; written his terror noted.
verses.before: For I have put my terror in the land of the living, and he will be laid among the uncircumcised with those slain by the sword— Pharaoh and all his multitude, declares the LORD GOD.
verses.after: For I spread my terror in the land of the living, and Pharaoh with all his multitude will be laid among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword, declares the Lord GOD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For I have put my terror in the land of the living, and he will be laid among the uncircumcised with those slain by the sword— Pharaoh and all his multitude, declares the LORD GOD.

verses.rationale: Retains recurring introduction.
verses.before: The word of the LORD came to me, saying:
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word of the LORD came to me, saying:

verses.rationale: Keeps divine initiative and chosen male watchman.
verses.before: “Human one, speak to your people and say to them: When I bring the sword against a land, and the people of that land take one man from among them and appoint him as their watchman,
verses.after: “Son of man, speak to your people. Tell them: Suppose I bring a sword against a land, and its people choose a man from among them and appoint him as their watchman.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Human one, speak to your people and say to them: When I bring the sword against a land, and the people of that land take one man from among them and appoint him as their watchman,

verses.rationale: Preserves warning sequence and ancient instrument.
verses.before: and he sees the sword coming against the land, blows the horn, and warns the people,
verses.after: He sees the sword approaching the land, blows the ram’s horn, and warns the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: and he sees the sword coming against the land, blows the horn, and warns the people,

verses.rationale: Keeps blood-accountability image with generic hearer.
verses.before: then anyone who hears the sound of the horn and does not take warning—if the sword comes and takes them away, their blood will be on their own head.
verses.after: If someone hears the horn but ignores the warning, and the sword comes and takes that person away, their blood will be on their own head.
verses.tsw_comparator: then anyone who hears the sound of the horn and does not take warning—if the sword comes and takes them away, their blood will be on their own head.

verses.rationale: Retains repetition and alternative outcome.
verses.before: They heard the sound of the horn and did not take warning; their blood will be on them. But one who takes warning will save their life.
verses.after: They heard the horn but ignored the warning; their blood will be their own responsibility. Had they heeded the warning, they would have saved their life.
verses.tsw_comparator: They heard the sound of the horn and did not take warning; their blood will be on them. But one who takes warning will save their life.

verses.rationale: Preserves both personal guilt and watchman's accountability.
verses.before: “But if the watchman sees the sword coming and does not blow the horn, so that the people are not warned, and the sword comes and takes one life from among them, that person is taken away in their guilt; but I will require their blood from the watchman’s hand.
verses.after: But if the watchman sees the sword coming and does not blow the horn, so the people receive no warning, and the sword comes and takes a life, that person is taken in their guilt. Yet I will demand their blood from the watchman’s hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: “But if the watchman sees the sword coming and does not blow the horn, so that the people are not warned, and the sword comes and takes one life from among them, that person is taken away in their guilt; but I will require their blood from the watchman’s hand.

verses.rationale: Connects image directly to Ezekiel's commission.
verses.before: “Now you, human one: I have appointed you as a watchman for the house of Israel. When you hear a word from my mouth, you must warn them from me.
verses.after: “You, son of man, I have appointed as a watchman for the house of Israel. Hear the word from my mouth and give them my warning.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Now you, human one: I have appointed you as a watchman for the house of Israel. When you hear a word from my mouth, you must warn them from me.

verses.rationale: Keeps quoted warning and repeated accountability.
verses.before: When I say to the wicked, ‘Wicked one, you will surely die,’ and you do not speak to warn the wicked away from their way, that wicked person will die in their guilt, but I will require their blood from your hand.
verses.after: When I tell the wicked, ‘Wicked one, you will surely die,’ and you do not speak to warn them away from their way, that wicked person will die in their guilt. But I will demand their blood from your hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: When I say to the wicked, ‘Wicked one, you will surely die,’ and you do not speak to warn the wicked away from their way, that wicked person will die in their guilt, but I will require their blood from your hand.

verses.rationale: Preserves contrast of response and messenger responsibility.
verses.before: But if you warn the wicked to turn from their way, and they do not turn from their way, they will die in their guilt; but you will have saved your life.
verses.after: But if you warn the wicked to turn from their way, and they do not turn from it, they will die in their guilt, while you will have saved your own life.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you warn the wicked to turn from their way, and they do not turn from their way, they will die in their guilt; but you will have saved your life.

verses.rationale: Keeps people's despair as direct speech.
verses.before: “And you, human one, say to the house of Israel: This is what you have said: ‘Surely our rebellions and our sins are upon us, and because of them we are wasting away. How then can we live?’
verses.after: “Son of man, tell the house of Israel: You say, ‘Our rebellions and sins weigh on us, and we are wasting away because of them. How can we live?’
verses.tsw_comparator: “And you, human one, say to the house of Israel: This is what you have said: ‘Surely our rebellions and our sins are upon us, and because of them we are wasting away. How then can we live?’

verses.rationale: Retains oath, doubled invitation and final question.
verses.before: Say to them: As I live, declares the LORD GOD, I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but instead that the wicked turn from their way and live. Turn back, turn back from your evil ways! Why should you die, house of Israel?
verses.after: Tell them: As I live, declares the Lord GOD, I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but in the wicked turning from their way and living. Turn back, turn back from your evil ways! Why should you die, house of Israel?
verses.tsw_comparator: Say to them: As I live, declares the LORD GOD, I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but rather that the wicked turn from their way and live. Turn back, turn back from your evil ways! Why should you die, house of Israel?

verses.rationale: Keeps all three claims without doctrinal expansion.
verses.before: “And you, human one, say to your people: The righteousness of the righteous will not save them on the day of their rebellion, and the wickedness of the wicked will not cause them to stumble on the day they turn from their wickedness. Nor will the righteous be able to live by their righteousness on the day they sin.
verses.after: “Son of man, tell your people: The righteousness of the righteous will not rescue them when they rebel. The wickedness of the wicked will not bring them down when they turn from it. A righteous person cannot live by past righteousness when they sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And you, human one, say to your people: The righteousness of the righteous will not save them on the day of their rebellion, and the wickedness of the wicked will not cause them to stumble on the day they turn from their wickedness. Nor will the righteous be able to live by their righteousness on the day they sin.

verses.rationale: Follows read-form plural deeds and causal conclusion.
verses.before: When I say to the righteous, ‘They will surely live,’ and they trust in their righteousness and do injustice, none of their righteous deeds will be remembered; because of the injustice they have done, they will die.
verses.after: When I tell the righteous that they will surely live, but they trust in their righteousness and do wrong, none of their righteous deeds will be remembered. They will die because of the wrong they have done.
verses.tsw_comparator: When I say to the righteous, ‘They will surely live,’ and they trust in their righteousness and do injustice, none of their righteous deeds will be remembered; because of the injustice they have done, they will die.

verses.rationale: Leaves conditional sentence continuing across verse labels.
verses.before: But when I say to the wicked, ‘You will surely die,’ and they turn from their sin and do justice and righteousness—
verses.after: But when I tell the wicked, ‘You will surely die,’ and they turn from their sin and do what is just and right—
verses.tsw_comparator: But when I say to the wicked, ‘You will surely die,’ and they turn from their sin and do justice and righteousness—

verses.rationale: Keeps practical restitution and emphatic survival.
verses.before: if the wicked restore a pledge, repay what they have taken by robbery, and walk in the statutes of life without doing injustice—they will surely live; they will not die.
verses.after: returning what was taken as a pledge, repaying what was stolen, and following the statutes that give life without doing wrong—they will surely live. They will not die.
verses.tsw_comparator: if the wicked restore a pledge, repay what they have taken by robbery, and walk in the statutes of life without doing injustice—they will surely live; they will not die.

verses.rationale: Retains read-form sins and repeated assurance.
verses.before: None of the sins they have committed will be remembered against them. They have done justice and righteousness; they will surely live.
verses.after: None of the sins they committed will be remembered against them. They have done what is just and right; they will surely live.
verses.tsw_comparator: None of the sins they have committed will be remembered against them. They have done justice and righteousness; they will surely live.

verses.rationale: Preserves accusation and reversed judgment.
verses.before: “Yet your people say, ‘The way of the LORD is not right,’ when it is their way that is not right.
verses.after: “Yet your people say, ‘The Lord’s way is not fair.’ It is their own way that is not fair.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Yet your people say, ‘The way of the LORD is not right,’ when it is their way that is not right.

verses.rationale: Keeps changed conduct as stated cause.
verses.before: When the righteous turn from their righteousness and do injustice, they will die because of it.
verses.after: When the righteous turn from their righteousness and do wrong, they will die because of it.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the righteous turn from their righteousness and do injustice, they will die because of it.

verses.rationale: Maintains parallel reversal of previous verse.
verses.before: But when the wicked turn from their wickedness and do justice and righteousness, because of these they will live.
verses.after: When the wicked turn from their wickedness and do what is just and right, they will live because of it.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when the wicked turn from their wickedness and do justice and righteousness, because of these they will live.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated complaint and individual judgment.
verses.before: Yet you say, ‘The way of the LORD is not right.’ House of Israel, I will judge each of you according to your ways.”
verses.after: Yet you say, ‘The Lord’s way is not fair.’ House of Israel, I will judge each of you according to your ways.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet you say, ‘The way of the LORD is not right.’ House of Israel, I will judge each of you according to your ways.”

verses.rationale: Retains pinned twelfth year and exiles' shared perspective.
verses.before: In the twelfth year of our exile, in the tenth month, on the fifth day of the month, a fugitive from Jerusalem came to me, saying, “The city has been struck down.”
verses.after: In the twelfth year of our exile, on the fifth day of the tenth month, a fugitive from Jerusalem came to me and said, “The city has fallen!”
verses.tsw_comparator: In the twelfth year of our exile, in the tenth month, on the fifth day of the month, a fugitive from Jerusalem came to me, saying, “The city has been struck down.”

verses.rationale: Preserves doubled opened-mouth report and timing.
verses.before: Now the hand of the LORD had been upon me in the evening, before the fugitive came. He opened my mouth before the man came to me in the morning; my mouth was opened, and I was no longer mute.
verses.after: The evening before the fugitive arrived, the hand of the LORD had come upon me. He opened my mouth before the man came to me in the morning. My mouth was opened, and I was no longer silent.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the hand of the LORD had been upon me in the evening, before the fugitive came. He opened my mouth before the man came to me in the morning; my mouth was opened, and I was no longer mute.

verses.rationale: Marks subsequent oracle.
verses.before: The word of the LORD came to me, saying:
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word of the LORD came to me, saying:

verses.rationale: Keeps their comparison as their own claim.
verses.before: “Human one, the inhabitants of these ruins on the land of Israel are saying, ‘Abraham was one man, yet he possessed the land; but we are many, and the land has been given to us as a possession.’

verses.tsw_comparator: You have not strengthened the weak, healed the sick, bound up the injured, brought back the straying, or sought the lost. Instead, you have ruled them with force and harshness.

verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD GOD: Look, I myself will search for my flock and examine them.

verses.rationale: Retains simile and cloud-darkness setting.
verses.before: As a shepherd examines their flock on the day when they are among their scattered sheep, so I will examine my flock. I will rescue them from all the places to which they were scattered on a day of cloud and deep darkness.
verses.after: As a shepherd looks after a flock when he is among his scattered sheep, so I will look after my flock. I will rescue them from every place where they were scattered on a day of cloud and thick darkness.
verses.tsw_comparator: As a shepherd examines their flock on the day when they are among their scattered sheep, so I will examine my flock. I will rescue them from all the places to which they were scattered on a day of cloud and deep darkness.

verses.rationale: Keeps gathering stages and three feeding locations.

verses.after: I will bring them out from the peoples, gather them from the lands, and bring them to their own soil. I will feed them on Israel’s mountains, in the ravines, and in all the inhabited places of the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will bring them out from the peoples and gather them from the lands, and I will bring them into their own land. I will shepherd them on the mountains of Israel, by the ravines, and in all the inhabited places of the land.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated good pasture and mountains.

verses.after: I will feed them in good pasture, and Israel’s high mountains will be their grazing land. There they will lie down in good grazing land and feed on rich pasture on Israel’s mountains.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will shepherd them in good pasture, and their fold will be on the high mountains of Israel. There they will lie down in a good fold, and they will feed in rich pasture on the mountains of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains doubled emphatic I.
verses.before: I myself will shepherd my flock, and I myself will make them lie down, declares the LORD GOD.
verses.after: I myself will feed my flock, and I myself will let them lie down, declares the Lord GOD.
verses.tsw_comparator: I myself will shepherd my flock, and I myself will make them lie down, declares the LORD GOD.

verses.rationale: Keeps pinned destroy, not emended protect.

verses.after: I will search for the lost, bring back the strays, bind up the injured, and strengthen the sick. But I will destroy the fat and the strong. I will feed them with justice.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will seek the lost, bring back the straying, bind up the injured, and strengthen the sick; but I will destroy the fat and the strong. I will shepherd it with justice.

verses.rationale: Preserves judgment within the flock and male animals.
verses.before: As for you, my flock, thus says the LORD GOD: Look, I am judging between one sheep and another, between rams and male goats.
verses.after: “As for you, my flock, this is what the Lord GOD says: I will judge between one sheep and another, between rams and male goats.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for you, my flock, thus says the LORD GOD: Look, I am judging between one sheep and another, between rams and male goats.

verses.rationale: Unfolds paired rhetorical questions without losing acts.

verses.tsw_comparator: Is it too little for you to feed in the good pasture, that you must trample the rest of your pasture with your feet? And to drink clear water, that you must foul what remains with your feet?

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated feet and victims' plight.

verses.tsw_comparator: Must my flock feed on what your feet have trampled and drink what your feet have fouled?

verses.rationale: Retains bodily violence within flock.

verses.tsw_comparator: I will save my flock, and they will no longer be plunder. I will judge between one sheep and another.

verses.tsw_comparator: They will no longer be plunder for the nations, nor will the wild animals of the land devour them. They will live securely, with no one to terrify them.

verses.before: And you, mortal, prophesy to the mountains of Israel, and say: Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the LORD.
verses.after: “Son of man, prophesy to Israel’s mountains. Say: Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the LORD!
verses.tsw_comparator: And you, mortal, prophesy to the mountains of Israel, and say: Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves enemy's boast and ancient heights.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD GOD: Because the enemy has said of you, “Aha! The ancient high places have become our possession,”
verses.after: This is what the Lord GOD says: The enemy said about you, ‘Aha! The ancient heights have become ours to possess.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD GOD: Because the enemy has said of you, “Aha! The ancient high places have become our possession,”

verses.rationale: Keeps accumulating reasons across verse boundary.
verses.before: so prophesy and say: Thus says the LORD GOD: Because they have made you desolate and snapped at you from every side, so that you became a possession for the remnant of the nations, and you have become the talk on people’s lips and their slander,
verses.after: Therefore prophesy and say: This is what the Lord GOD says: Because they ravaged and crushed you from every side, making you a possession for the remaining nations, and because people made you a subject of gossip and slander,
verses.tsw_comparator: therefore prophesy and say: Thus says the LORD GOD: Because they have made you desolate and snapped at you from every side, so that you became a possession for the remnant of the nations, and you have become the talk on people’s lips and their slander,

verses.rationale: Preserves full addressed landscape and both titles.
verses.before: so, mountains of Israel, hear the word of the LORD GOD. Thus says the LORD GOD to the mountains and the hills, to the ravines and the valleys, to the desolate ruins and the abandoned cities that have become plunder and mockery to the remnant of the nations all around.
verses.after: therefore, mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD! This is what the Lord GOD says to the mountains and hills, ravines and valleys, desolate ruins and abandoned cities that became plunder and a mockery to the remaining nations all around:
verses.tsw_comparator: therefore, mountains of Israel, hear the word of the LORD GOD. Thus says the LORD GOD to the mountains and the hills, to the ravines and the valleys, to the desolate ruins and the abandoned cities that have become plunder and mockery to the remnant of the nations all around.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine land claim and difficult pasture term.
verses.before: So thus says the LORD GOD: Surely in the fire of my jealousy I have spoken against the remnant of the nations and against all Edom, who gave my land to themselves as a possession with wholehearted joy and contempt of soul, in order to make its pastureland plunder.
verses.after: This is what the Lord GOD says: In the fire of my jealousy I have spoken against the remaining nations and all Edom, who took my land as their own possession with wholehearted joy and contempt, making its pastureland plunder.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus says the LORD GOD: Surely in the fire of my jealousy I have spoken against the remnant of the nations and against all Edom, who gave my land to themselves as a possession with wholehearted joy and contempt of soul, in order to make its pastureland plunder.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated landscape and reason for speech.
verses.before: So prophesy concerning the land of Israel, and say to the mountains and the hills, to the ravines and the valleys: Thus says the LORD GOD: Look, I have spoken in my jealousy and in my wrath, because you have borne the disgrace of the nations.
verses.after: Therefore prophesy over Israel’s soil. Tell the mountains and hills, ravines and valleys: This is what the Lord GOD says: I have spoken in my jealousy and fury because you have borne the nations’ disgrace.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore prophesy concerning the land of Israel, and say to the mountains and the hills, to the ravines and the valleys: Thus says the LORD GOD: Look, I have spoken in my jealousy and in my wrath, because you have borne the disgrace of the nations.

verses.rationale: Makes oath gesture understandable while retaining it.
verses.before: So thus says the LORD GOD: I have raised my hand in oath: Surely the nations around you will bear their own disgrace.
verses.after: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I have raised my hand in an oath: the nations around you will bear their own disgrace.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus says the LORD GOD: I have raised my hand in oath: Surely the nations around you will bear their own disgrace.

verses.rationale: Keeps land fertility for approaching people.
verses.before: But you, mountains of Israel, will put forth your branches and bear your fruit for my people Israel, for they are near to come.
verses.after: “But you, mountains of Israel, will put out branches and bear fruit for my people Israel, for they are coming soon.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you, mountains of Israel, will put forth your branches and bear your fruit for my people Israel, for they are near to come.

verses.rationale: Preserves reversal from against-you formulas.
verses.before: For look, I am for you, and I will turn toward you; you will be cultivated and sown.
verses.after: I am for you. I will turn toward you, and you will be tilled and sown.
verses.tsw_comparator: For look, I am for you, and I will turn toward you; you will be cultivated and sown.

verses.rationale: Keeps emphatic whole-house formulation.
verses.before: I will multiply people upon you—all the house of Israel, all of it. The cities will be inhabited, and the ruins rebuilt.
verses.after: I will multiply people on you, the whole house of Israel, all of it. The cities will be inhabited and the ruins rebuilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will multiply people upon you—all the house of Israel, all of it. The cities will be inhabited, and the ruins rebuilt.

verses.rationale: Preserves animal restoration and better-than-before promise.
verses.before: I will multiply upon you people and animals; they will multiply and be fruitful. I will cause you to be inhabited as in your former times, and I will do you more good than in your beginnings. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
verses.after: I will multiply humans and animals on you; they will increase and be fruitful. I will make you inhabited as before and treat you better than at the beginning. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will multiply upon you people and animals; they will multiply and be fruitful. I will cause you to be inhabited as in your former times, and I will do you more good than in your beginnings. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains land personification and bereavement.
verses.before: I will cause people to walk upon you—my people Israel—and they will possess you. You will be their inheritance, and you will no longer make them childless.
verses.after: I will bring people to walk on you, my people Israel. They will possess you, and you will be their inheritance. You will never again bereave them of children.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will cause people to walk upon you—my people Israel—and they will possess you. You will be their inheritance, and you will no longer make them childless.

verses.rationale: Keeps read-form plural nations and accusation.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD GOD: Because they say to you, “You devour people, and you have made your nation childless,”
verses.after: “This is what the Lord GOD says: People say to you, ‘You devour human beings and bereave your nations.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD GOD: Because they say to you, “You devour people, and you have made your nation childless,”

verses.rationale: Follows read-form bereave distinct from stumbling.
verses.before: so you will no longer devour people, and you will no longer cause your nation to stumble, declares the LORD GOD.
verses.after: Therefore you will no longer devour human beings or bereave your nations, declares the Lord GOD.
verses.tsw_comparator: therefore you will no longer devour people, and you will no longer cause your nation to stumble, declares the LORD GOD.

verses.rationale: Preserves stumbling verb rather than harmonizing bereave.
verses.before: I will no longer let you hear the disgrace of the nations, nor will you bear the reproach of peoples anymore; and you will no longer cause your nation to stumble, declares the LORD GOD.
verses.after: I will no longer let you hear the nations’ insults. You will no longer bear the peoples’ taunts or cause your nations to stumble, declares the Lord GOD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will no longer let you hear the disgrace of the nations, nor will you bear the reproach of peoples anymore; and you will no longer cause your nation to stumble, declares the LORD GOD.

verses.rationale: Marks new explanation.
verses.before: The word of the LORD came to me:
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word of the LORD came to me:

verses.rationale: Keeps ritual bodily comparison with explanatory note.
verses.before: Mortal, when the house of Israel lived in their land, they defiled it by their way and their deeds. Their way before me was like the uncleanness of a menstruating woman.
verses.after: “Son of man, when the house of Israel lived on their own soil, they defiled it by their ways and deeds. Their conduct before me was like menstrual uncleanness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Mortal, when the house of Israel lived in their land, they defiled it by their way and their deeds. Their way before me was like the uncleanness of a menstruating woman.

verses.rationale: Preserves bloodshed and idols as distinct causes.
verses.before: So I poured out my wrath upon them for the blood that they had shed on the land, and because they had defiled it with their idols.
verses.after: So I poured out my fury on them for the blood they shed on the land and for defiling it with their idols.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I poured out my wrath upon them for the blood that they had shed on the land, and because they had defiled it with their idols.

verses.rationale: Keeps conduct as measure of judgment.
verses.before: I scattered them among the nations, and they were dispersed through the lands. I judged them according to their way and their deeds.
verses.after: I scattered them among the nations, and they were dispersed through the lands. I judged them according to their ways and deeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: I scattered them among the nations, and they were dispersed through the lands. I judged them according to their way and their deeds.

verses.rationale: Makes quoted reputational consequence explicit.
verses.before: When they came to the nations where they went, they profaned my holy name, when people said of them, “These are the people of the LORD, yet they had to leave his land.”
verses.after: Wherever they went among the nations, they profaned my holy name. People said of them, ‘These are the LORD’s people, yet they had to leave his land.’
verses.tsw_comparator: When they came to the nations where they went, they profaned my holy name, when people said of them, “These are the people of the LORD, yet they had to leave his land.”

verses.rationale: Retains divine name as stated concern.
verses.before: Yet I had concern for my holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the nations where they went.
verses.after: But I had concern for my holy name, which the house of Israel profaned among the nations where they went.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I had concern for my holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the nations where they went.

verses.rationale: Keeps explicit negative and positive motive.
verses.before: So say to the house of Israel: Thus says the LORD GOD: It is not for your sake that I am acting, house of Israel, but for my holy name, which you have profaned among the nations where you went.
verses.after: “Therefore tell the house of Israel: This is what the Lord GOD says: I am acting for the sake of my holy name, which you profaned among the nations where you went—not for your sake, house of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore say to the house of Israel: Thus says the LORD GOD: It is not for your sake that I am acting, house of Israel, but for my holy name, which you have profaned among the nations where you went.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated profanation and international recognition.
verses.before: I will sanctify my great name, which has been profaned among the nations, which you have profaned among them. Then the nations will know that I am the LORD, declares the LORD GOD, when I show myself holy through you before their eyes.
verses.after: I will show the holiness of my great name, profaned among the nations, which you profaned among them. The nations will know that I am the LORD, declares the Lord GOD, when I show myself holy through you before their eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will sanctify my great name, which has been profaned among the nations, which you have profaned among them. Then the nations will know that I am the LORD, declares the LORD GOD, when I show myself holy through you before their eyes.

verses.rationale: Keeps three movements of return.
verses.before: For I will take you from the nations, gather you from all the lands, and bring you into your own land.
verses.after: I will take you from the nations, gather you from all the lands, and bring you to your own soil.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I will take you from the nations, gather you from all the lands, and bring you into your own land.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated cleansing and concrete sprinkling.
verses.before: I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean. From all your uncleannesses and from all your idols I will cleanse you.
verses.after: I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean. I will cleanse you from all your uncleanness and all your idols.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean. From all your uncleannesses and from all your idols I will cleanse you.

verses.rationale: Keeps both flesh references and new heart/spirit distinction.
verses.before: I will give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you. I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.
verses.after: I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you. I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you. I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine causation and ensuing conduct.
verses.before: I will put my Spirit within you, and I will make it happen that you walk in my statutes, keep my judgments, and do them.
verses.after: I will put my spirit within you and cause you to follow my statutes, keeping my judgments and carrying them out.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will put my Spirit within you, and I will make it happen that you walk in my statutes, keep my judgments, and do them.

verses.rationale: Keeps ancestral land and covenant relationship formula.
verses.before: You will live in the land that I gave to your ancestors. You will be my people, and I will be your God.
verses.after: You will live in the land I gave your ancestors. You will be my people, and I will be your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will live in the land that I gave to your ancestors. You will be my people, and I will be your God.

verses.rationale: Retains summoning grain as personified command.
verses.before: I will save you from all your uncleannesses. I will call for the grain and make it plentiful, and I will not bring famine upon you.
verses.after: I will save you from all your uncleanness. I will summon the grain and make it abundant, and I will bring no famine upon you.
