verses.rationale: Renders three/thirty arrangement provisionally, preserving separate support.
verses.before: The side chambers were chamber beside chamber, thirty times over in three levels. They entered into the wall belonging to the house, around the side chambers, all around, so that they might be supported, but they were not supported by the wall of the house.
verses.after: The side chambers were arranged one above another in three stories, thirty in each. They rested on ledges in the wall surrounding the temple, so they could be supported without being fastened into the temple wall itself.
verses.tsw_comparator: The side chambers were chamber beside chamber, thirty times over in three levels. They entered into the wall belonging to the house, around the side chambers, all around, so that they might be supported, but they were not supported by the wall of the house.

verses.rationale: Keeps upward widening and middle-level access.
verses.before: The side chambers widened and went upward, story by story, because the structure of the house went upward, story by story, all around the house. Therefore the house became wider upward; and from the lowest level one went up to the highest through the middle level.
verses.after: The side chambers grew wider at each higher story, as the surrounding structure rose level by level. The width increased upward, and one went from the lowest level to the highest through the middle level.
verses.tsw_comparator: The side chambers widened and went upward, story by story, because the structure of the house went upward, story by story, all around the house. Therefore the house became wider upward; and from the lowest level one went up to the highest through the middle level.

verses.rationale: Keeps platform and full-reed height; term qualified.
verses.before: I saw that the house had a raised base all around. The foundations of the side chambers were a full rod, six cubits to the joint.
verses.after: I saw a raised platform all around the temple. The side chambers’ foundations measured a full reed, six long cubits.
verses.tsw_comparator: I saw that the house had a raised base all around. The foundations of the side chambers were a full rod, six cubits to the joint.

verses.rationale: Preserves wall/open-space distinction across verse boundary.
verses.before: The width of the outer wall of the side chamber was five cubits. The open space beside the side chambers belonging to the house—
verses.after: The outer wall of the side chambers was five cubits thick. There was an open space beside the temple’s side chambers,
verses.tsw_comparator: The width of the outer wall of the side chamber was five cubits. The open space beside the side chambers belonging to the house—

verses.rationale: Keeps twenty-cubit intervening space.
verses.before: and between the chambers—was twenty cubits wide, all around the house, all around.
verses.after: and between them and the chambers was a space twenty cubits wide all around the temple.
verses.tsw_comparator: and between the chambers—was twenty cubits wide, all around the house, all around.

verses.rationale: Preserves two entrances and five-cubit walkway.
verses.before: The doorway of the side chamber opened onto the open space: one doorway facing north and one doorway facing south. The width of the open space was five cubits, all around.
verses.after: The side chambers opened onto the open space, one entrance facing north and one facing south. The open space was five cubits wide all around.
verses.tsw_comparator: The doorway of the side chamber opened onto the open space: one doorway facing north and one doorway facing south. The width of the open space was five cubits, all around.

verses.rationale: Keeps west orientation and seventy/five/ninety.
verses.before: The building that faced the separate area on the western side was seventy cubits wide. The wall of the building was five cubits wide all around, and its length was ninety cubits.
verses.after: The building facing the separate area on the west was seventy cubits wide. Its wall was five cubits thick all around, and its length was ninety cubits.
verses.tsw_comparator: The building that faced the separate area on the western side was seventy cubits wide. The wall of the building was five cubits wide all around, and its length was ninety cubits.

verses.rationale: Retains two distinct hundred-cubit totals.
verses.before: He measured the house: one hundred cubits long. The separate area, the building, and its walls were one hundred cubits long.
verses.after: He measured the temple: a hundred cubits long. The separate area, the building, and its walls also measured a hundred cubits in length.
verses.tsw_comparator: He measured the house: one hundred cubits long. The separate area, the building, and its walls were one hundred cubits long.

verses.rationale: Keeps eastward width distinct from length.
verses.before: The width of the front of the house, together with the separate area toward the east, was one hundred cubits.
verses.after: The front of the temple and the separate area on the east measured a hundred cubits across.
verses.tsw_comparator: The width of the front of the house, together with the separate area toward the east, was one hundred cubits.

verses.rationale: Preserves galleries and continuing description.
verses.before: He measured the length of the building facing the separate area behind it, together with its galleries on this side and on that side: one hundred cubits. The inner temple hall and the porches of the court,
verses.after: He measured the building facing the separate area behind the temple, with its galleries on both sides: a hundred cubits. The inner hall and the court’s vestibules,
verses.tsw_comparator: He measured the length of the building facing the separate area behind it, together with its galleries on this side and on that side: one hundred cubits. The inner temple hall and the porches of the court,

verses.rationale: Keeps difficult three-part reference and wood coverage.
verses.before: the thresholds, the shuttered windows, and the galleries around the three levels—opposite the threshold—were paneled with wood all around, from the ground to the windows; and the windows were covered.
verses.after: the thresholds, recessed windows, and galleries around all three were paneled with wood all around, opposite the threshold, from the floor to the windows. The windows were covered.
verses.tsw_comparator: the thresholds, the shuttered windows, and the galleries around the three levels—opposite the threshold—were paneled with wood all around, from the ground to the windows; and the windows were covered.

verses.rationale: Retains measured wording rather than replacing with carving.
verses.before: Above the doorway, as far as the inner house, and outside, on every wall all around, inside and outside, were measurements.
verses.after: Above the entrance, inside the temple and outside, along every wall inside and outside, everything was measured.
verses.tsw_comparator: Above the doorway, as far as the inner house, and outside, on every wall all around, inside and outside, were measurements.

verses.rationale: Keeps two-faced rather than earlier four-faced creatures.
verses.before: Cherubim and palm trees were made, with a palm tree between cherub and cherub. Each cherub had two faces:
verses.after: Cherubim and palm trees were carved there, a palm between each pair of cherubim. Each cherub had two faces:
verses.tsw_comparator: Cherubim and palm trees were made, with a palm tree between cherub and cherub. Each cherub had two faces:

verses.rationale: Preserves both face identities and orientation.
verses.before: a human face toward the palm tree on this side, and a young lion’s face toward the palm tree on that side. They were made throughout the whole house, all around.
verses.after: a human face toward the palm on one side and a young lion’s face toward the palm on the other. They were carved all around the temple.
verses.tsw_comparator: a human face toward the palm tree on this side, and a young lion’s face toward the palm tree on that side. They were made throughout the whole house, all around.

verses.rationale: Retains dotted source clause as received.
verses.before: From the ground up to above the doorway, cherubim and palm trees were made—and the wall of the temple hall.
verses.after: From the floor to above the entrance, cherubim and palm trees were carved on the wall of the main hall.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the ground up to above the doorway, cherubim and palm trees were made—and the wall of the temple hall.

verses.rationale: Keeps square posts and obscure comparison.
verses.before: The doorposts of the temple hall were square, and the appearance of the front of the sanctuary was like the appearance of the other.
verses.after: The main hall’s doorposts were square. The front of the sanctuary had the same appearance.
verses.tsw_comparator: The doorposts of the temple hall were square, and the appearance of the front of the sanctuary was like the appearance of the other.

verses.rationale: Retains altar/table naming and unusual length wording.
verses.before: The wooden altar was three cubits high and two cubits long. Its corners, its length, and its sides were of wood. He said to me, “This is the table that is before the LORD.”
verses.after: The wooden altar was three cubits high and two cubits long. Its corners, its length, and its sides were wood. He told me, “This is the table that stands before the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The wooden altar was three cubits high and two cubits long. Its corners, its length, and its sides were of wood. He said to me, “This is the table that is before the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Keeps paired doors for both spaces.
verses.before: The temple hall and the sanctuary had two doors.
verses.after: The main hall and the sanctuary each had double doors.
verses.tsw_comparator: The temple hall and the sanctuary had two doors.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated two-leaf construction.
verses.before: The doors had two swinging leaves each: two leaves for one door and two leaves for the other.
verses.after: Each door had two swinging leaves, two leaves for one door and two for the other.
verses.tsw_comparator: The doors had two swinging leaves each: two leaves for one door and two leaves for the other.

verses.rationale: Uses canopy provisionally; preserves matching ornament.
verses.before: Cherubim and palm trees were made on the doors of the temple hall, like those made on the walls. A wooden canopy was on the front of the porch outside.
verses.after: Cherubim and palm trees were carved on the doors of the main hall, as on the walls. A wooden canopy stood across the outside front of the vestibule.
verses.tsw_comparator: Cherubim and palm trees were made on the doors of the temple hall, like those made on the walls. A wooden canopy was on the front of the porch outside.

verses.rationale: Keeps difficult concluding architectural inventory.
verses.before: There were shuttered windows and palm trees on this side and on that side, on the sides of the porch, the side chambers of the house, and the canopies.
verses.after: Recessed windows and palm trees stood on both sides of the vestibule, along with the temple’s side chambers and the canopies.
verses.tsw_comparator: There were shuttered windows and palm trees on this side and on that side, on the sides of the porch, the side chambers of the house, and the canopies.

verses.rationale: Keeps movement and opposing structures.
verses.before: Then he brought me out to the outer court by way of the north, and brought me to the chamber that was opposite the separate area and opposite the building, toward the north.
verses.after: He led me north into the outer court and brought me to the chambers opposite the separate area and the building on the north.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he brought me out to the outer court by way of the north, and brought me to the chamber that was opposite the separate area and opposite the building, toward the north.

verses.rationale: Preserves dimensions and doorway direction.
verses.before: Its length along the front was one hundred cubits, with an entrance on the north; and its width was fifty cubits.
verses.after: The building was a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide, with an entrance on the north.
verses.tsw_comparator: Its length along the front was one hundred cubits, with an entrance on the north; and its width was fifty cubits.

verses.rationale: Keeps twenty-cubit reference and three levels.
verses.before: Opposite the twenty cubits belonging to the inner court, and opposite the pavement belonging to the outer court, gallery faced gallery on the third level.
verses.after: Facing the twenty-cubit space beside the inner court and the outer court’s pavement, galleries faced galleries on three levels.
verses.tsw_comparator: Opposite the twenty cubits belonging to the inner court, and opposite the pavement belonging to the outer court, gallery faced gallery on the third level.

verses.rationale: Retains difficult one-cubit measure rather than emending hundred.
verses.before: In front of the chambers was a passage, ten cubits wide, leading inward; a path one cubit wide; and their entrances faced north.
verses.after: Before the chambers was a passage ten cubits wide toward the interior, with a way one cubit wide. Their doors faced north.
verses.tsw_comparator: In front of the chambers was a passage, ten cubits wide, leading inward; a path one cubit wide; and their entrances faced north.

verses.rationale: Keeps galleries as cause of reduced width.
verses.before: The upper chambers were shortened, because the galleries took away from them more than from the lower and middle levels of the building.
verses.after: The upper chambers were narrower because the galleries took more space from them than from the lower and middle stories.
verses.tsw_comparator: The upper chambers were shortened, because the galleries took away from them more than from the lower and middle levels of the building.

verses.rationale: Preserves lack of supporting pillars.
verses.before: For they were three stories, and they had no pillars like the pillars of the courts; therefore they were set back from the ground, more than the lower and middle levels.
verses.after: There were three stories, without pillars like those of the courts. So the upper story was set back from the lower and middle stories above the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: For they were three stories, and they had no pillars like the pillars of the courts; therefore they were set back from the ground, more than the lower and middle levels.

verses.rationale: Keeps fifty-cubit exterior wall.
verses.before: There was a wall outside, alongside the chambers, toward the outer court, facing the chambers. Its length was fifty cubits.
verses.after: An outer wall ran along the chambers toward the outer court, in front of them, for fifty cubits.
verses.tsw_comparator: There was a wall outside, alongside the chambers, toward the outer court, facing the chambers. Its length was fifty cubits.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes shorter and longer rows.
verses.before: For the length of the chambers toward the outer court was fifty cubits, but there before the temple it was one hundred cubits.
verses.after: The row of chambers facing the outer court was fifty cubits long, while the row facing the temple was a hundred cubits.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the length of the chambers toward the outer court was fifty cubits, but there before the temple it was one hundred cubits.

verses.rationale: Follows read-form segmentation without reconstructing walls.
verses.before: Below these chambers was an entrance from the east, for one entering them from the outer court.
verses.after: Below these chambers was the east entrance used by those coming in from the outer court.
verses.tsw_comparator: Below these chambers was an entrance from the east, for one entering them from the outer court.

verses.rationale: Retains pinned east, alternative south noted.
verses.before: In the width of the court wall, toward the east, opposite the separate area and opposite the building, were chambers.
verses.after: Within the width of the court’s wall on the east were chambers facing the separate area and the building.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the width of the court wall, toward the east, opposite the separate area and opposite the building, were chambers.

verses.rationale: Keeps all five points of correspondence.
verses.before: A path lay before them, like the appearance of the chambers that faced north: their length was the same as their width, and so were all their exits, their arrangements, and their entrances.
verses.after: A passage ran before them. They resembled the northern chambers in length and width, exits, arrangements, and entrances.
verses.tsw_comparator: A path lay before them, like the appearance of the chambers that faced north: their length was the same as their width, and so were all their exits, their arrangements, and their entrances.

verses.rationale: Preserves difficult corresponding-wall phrase provisionally.
verses.before: As were the entrances of the chambers that faced south, there was an entrance at the head of the path—the path before the wall, the wall facing east—for those entering them.
verses.after: Like the entrances of the southern chambers, there was an entrance at the head of the passage, beside the corresponding wall, for those entering from the east.
verses.tsw_comparator: As were the entrances of the chambers that faced south, there was an entrance at the head of the path—the path before the wall, the wall facing east—for those entering them.

verses.rationale: Keeps three offering types and repeated holiness.
verses.before: Then he said to me, “The north chambers and the south chambers, which face the separate area, are holy chambers. There the priests who draw near to the LORD will eat the most holy offerings. There they will place the most holy offerings, the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering, because the place is holy.
verses.after: He told me, “The northern and southern chambers facing the separate area are holy chambers. There the priests who approach the LORD will eat the most holy offerings. There they will place the most holy offerings—the grain offering, sin offering, and guilt offering—for the place is holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said to me, “The north chambers and the south chambers, which face the separate area, are holy chambers. There the priests who draw near to the LORD shall eat the most holy offerings. There they shall place the most holy offerings, the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering, because the place is holy.

verses.rationale: Keeps change of garments tied to holy status.
verses.before: “When the priests enter, they will not go out from the holy place into the outer court. There they will leave the garments in which they minister, for they are holy; they will clothe themselves and put on other garments, and then they may approach what belongs to the people.”
verses.after: When the priests enter, they must not go straight from the holy place into the outer court. They must leave their service garments there, because they are holy, and put on other clothes before approaching the people’s area.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “When the priests enter, they shall not go out from the holy place into the outer court. There they shall leave the garments in which they minister, for they are holy; they shall clothe themselves and put on other garments, and then they may approach what belongs to the people.”

verses.rationale: Preserves transition from interior to perimeter.
verses.before: When he had finished measuring the inner temple, he brought me out by way of the gate that faced east, and he measured it all around.
verses.after: When he finished measuring the inner temple, he led me out through the east-facing gate and measured the surrounding area.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he had finished measuring the inner temple, he brought me out by way of the gate that faced east, and he measured it all around.

verses.rationale: Follows read-form hundred, preserves reeds as unit.
verses.before: He measured the east side with the measuring reed: five cubits, one hundred reeds, by the measuring reed, all around.
verses.after: He measured all along the east side with the measuring reed: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed.
verses.tsw_comparator: He measured the east side with the measuring reed: five cubits, one hundred reeds, by the measuring reed, all around.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated northern measure.
verses.before: He measured the north side: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed, all around.
verses.after: He measured the north side: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed.
verses.tsw_comparator: He measured the north side: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed, all around.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated southern measure.
verses.before: He measured the south side: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed.
verses.after: He measured the south side: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed.
verses.tsw_comparator: He measured the south side: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed.

verses.rationale: Keeps west completing four sides.
verses.before: He turned to the west side and measured: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed.
verses.after: He turned to the west side and measured five hundred reeds by the measuring reed.
verses.tsw_comparator: He turned to the west side and measured: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed.

verses.rationale: Keeps unsupplied final unit and stated separation purpose.
verses.before: He measured it on its four sides. It had a wall all around, five hundred long and five hundred wide, to separate between what is holy and what is common.
verses.after: He measured all four sides. A wall surrounded it, five hundred long and five hundred wide, separating the holy from the common.
verses.tsw_comparator: He measured it on its four sides. It had a wall all around, five hundred long and five hundred wide, to separate between what is holy and what is common.

verses.rationale: Keeps orientation of returning glory.
verses.before: Then he led me to the gate, the gate that faces east.
verses.after: He led me to the gate facing east.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he led me to the gate, the gate that faces east.

verses.rationale: Preserves voice/waters comparison and illumination.
verses.before: And there—the glory of the God of Israel was coming from the east. His voice was like the sound of many waters, and the earth shone from his glory.
verses.after: The glory of the God of Israel was coming from the east. His voice was like the sound of great waters, and the earth shone with his glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: And there—the glory of the God of Israel was coming from the east. His voice was like the sound of many waters, and the earth shone from his glory.

verses.rationale: Retains pinned I came, with variant note.
verses.before: The vision I saw was like the vision I had seen when he came to destroy the city, and the visions were like the vision I had seen by the Kebar River. I fell facedown.
verses.after: The vision looked like the one I had seen when I came to destroy the city, and like the visions I had seen beside the Kebar River. I fell facedown.
verses.tsw_comparator: The vision I saw was like the vision I had seen when he came to destroy the city, and the visions were like the vision I had seen by the Kebar River. I fell facedown.

verses.rationale: Preserves route of entry.
verses.before: The glory of the LORD entered the house by way of the gate that faces east.
verses.after: The glory of the LORD entered the temple through the east-facing gate.
verses.tsw_comparator: The glory of the LORD entered the house by way of the gate that faces east.

verses.rationale: Keeps distinct transport and filling actions.
verses.before: Then the Spirit lifted me and brought me into the inner court, and there—the glory of the LORD filled the house.
verses.after: The spirit lifted me and brought me into the inner court. The glory of the LORD filled the temple.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the Spirit lifted me and brought me into the inner court, and there—the glory of the LORD filled the house.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes speaker from accompanying man.
verses.before: I heard someone speaking to me from the house, while a man was standing beside me.
verses.after: I heard someone speaking to me from the temple while the man stood beside me.
verses.tsw_comparator: I heard someone speaking to me from the house, while a man was standing beside me.

verses.rationale: Keeps throne/feet and difficult royal-corpse clause.
verses.before: He said to me, “Human one, this is the place of my throne and the place for the soles of my feet, where I will dwell among the children of Israel forever. The house of Israel and their kings will no longer defile my holy name by their prostitution or by the corpses of their kings at their high places.
verses.after: He said, “Son of man, this is the place of my throne and the place for the soles of my feet, where I will dwell among the Israelites forever. The house of Israel and their kings will no longer defile my holy name by their prostitution or by the corpses of their kings at their high places.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to me, “Human one, this is the place of my throne and the place for the soles of my feet, where I will dwell among the children of Israel forever. The house of Israel and their kings will no longer defile my holy name by their prostitution or by the corpses of their kings at their high places.

verses.rationale: Preserves proximity and consequence.
verses.before: When they placed their threshold beside my threshold and their doorposts beside my doorposts, with only a wall between me and them, they defiled my holy name by the detestable things they did. So I consumed them in my anger.
verses.after: They set their threshold beside mine and their doorpost beside mine, with only a wall between me and them. They defiled my holy name by the abominations they committed, so I consumed them in my anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they placed their threshold beside my threshold and their doorposts beside my doorposts, with only a wall between me and them, they defiled my holy name by the detestable things they did. So I consumed them in my anger.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated removal and permanent dwelling.
verses.before: Now let them put their prostitution and the corpses of their kings far from me, and I will dwell among them forever.
verses.after: Now let them put their prostitution and their kings’ corpses far from me, and I will dwell among them forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now let them put their prostitution and the corpses of their kings far from me, and I will dwell among them forever.

verses.rationale: Retains measuring as commanded response.
verses.before: “You, human one, tell the house of Israel about the house, so that they may be ashamed of their iniquities. Let them measure the design.
verses.after: “Son of man, describe the temple to the house of Israel, so they may be ashamed of their guilt. Let them measure its design.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You, human one, tell the house of Israel about the house, so that they may be ashamed of their iniquities. Let them measure the design.

verses.rationale: Retains awkward repeated forms rather than deleting source words.
verses.before: If they are ashamed of all that they have done, reveal to them the form of the house and its arrangement, its exits and its entrances, all its forms, all its statutes, all its forms, and all its laws. Write them down before their eyes, so that they may keep its entire form and all its statutes and do them.
verses.after: If they are ashamed of all they have done, make known to them the temple’s form and arrangement, its exits and entrances, all its forms, all its statutes, all its forms and all its instructions. Write these before their eyes, so they may observe all its form and all its statutes and carry them out.
verses.tsw_comparator: If they are ashamed of all that they have done, make known to them the form of the house and its arrangement, its exits and its entrances, all its forms, all its statutes, all its forms, and all its laws. Write them down before their eyes, so that they may keep its entire form and all its statutes and do them.

verses.rationale: Preserves framing repetition.
verses.before: This is the law of the house: On the top of the mountain, all its territory around it is most holy. Look—this is the law of the house.
verses.after: This is the instruction for the temple: the whole area on top of the mountain, all around, is most holy. This is the instruction for the temple.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the law of the house: On the top of the mountain, all its territory around it is most holy. Look—this is the law of the house.

verses.rationale: Keeps unit definition and span distinct from cubit.
verses.before: “These are the measurements of the altar in cubits—the cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth: the gutter will be one cubit deep and one cubit wide, with a border around its edge one span. This will be the base of the altar.
verses.after: “These are the altar’s measurements in long cubits, each a cubit and a handbreadth. Its base is one cubit deep and one cubit wide, with a rim one span wide around its edge. This is the altar’s base.
verses.tsw_comparator: “These are the measurements of the altar in cubits—the cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth: the gutter shall be one cubit deep and one cubit wide, with a border around its edge one span. This shall be the base of the altar.

verses.rationale: Preserves staged heights and repeated widths.
verses.before: From the gutter at ground level to the lower ledge will be two cubits, with a width of one cubit; and from the smaller ledge to the larger ledge will be four cubits, with a width of one cubit.
verses.after: From the base on the ground to the lower ledge is two cubits, with a width of one cubit. From the smaller ledge to the larger ledge is four cubits, with a width of one cubit.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the gutter at ground level to the lower ledge shall be two cubits, with a width of one cubit; and from the smaller ledge to the larger ledge shall be four cubits, with a width of one cubit.

verses.rationale: Keeps height and horn count distinct.
verses.before: The altar hearth will be four cubits high, and from the altar hearth upward there will be four horns.
verses.after: The altar hearth is four cubits high, and four horns project upward from the hearth.
verses.tsw_comparator: The altar hearth shall be four cubits high, and from the altar hearth upward there shall be four horns.

verses.rationale: Preserves twelve-by-twelve square.
verses.before: The altar hearth will be twelve cubits long by twelve cubits wide, square on its four sides.
verses.after: The hearth is twelve cubits long and twelve cubits wide, square on its four sides.
verses.tsw_comparator: The altar hearth shall be twelve cubits long by twelve cubits wide, square on its four sides.

verses.rationale: Keeps fourteen, half, one and east orientation.
verses.before: The ledge will be fourteen cubits long by fourteen cubits wide on its four sides, with a border around it of half a cubit and a gutter around it of one cubit. Its steps will face east.”
verses.after: The ledge is fourteen cubits long and fourteen cubits wide on its four sides. Its surrounding rim is half a cubit, and its base extends one cubit all around. Its steps face east.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The ledge shall be fourteen cubits long by fourteen cubits wide on its four sides, with a border around it of half a cubit and a gutter around it of one cubit. Its steps shall face east.”

verses.rationale: Preserves altar rites and blood action.
verses.before: Then he said to me, “Human one, this is what the LORD GOD says: These are the statutes for the altar on the day it is made, to offer burnt offerings on it and to splash blood on it.
verses.after: He told me, “Son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says: These are the altar’s statutes for the day it is made, for offering burnt offerings on it and splashing blood against it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said to me, “Human one, this is what the LORD GOD says: These are the statutes for the altar on the day it is made, to offer burnt offerings on it and to splash blood on it.

verses.rationale: Keeps specific priestly lineage and animal.
verses.before: You will give to the Levitical priests who are from the offspring of Zadok, who draw near to me to minister to me, declares the LORD GOD, a bull from the herd as a sin offering.
verses.after: Give a young bull as a sin offering to the Levitical priests descended from Zadok, who approach me to serve me, declares the Lord GOD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall give to the Levitical priests who are from the offspring of Zadok, who draw near to me to minister to me, declares the LORD GOD, a bull from the herd as a sin offering.

verses.rationale: Keeps three blood locations and paired ritual verbs.
verses.before: You will take some of its blood and put it on its four horns, on the four corners of the ledge, and on the border all around. Thus you will cleanse it from sin and make atonement for it.
verses.after: Take some of its blood and put it on the altar’s four horns, the ledge’s four corners, and the rim all around. Purify the altar and make atonement for it.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall take some of its blood and put it on its four horns, on the four corners of the ledge, and on the border all around. Thus you shall cleanse it from sin and make atonement for it.

verses.rationale: Preserves external burning location.
verses.before: You will take the bull of the sin offering, and it will be burned in the appointed place of the house, outside the sanctuary.
verses.after: Take the bull of the sin offering and burn it at the temple’s appointed place outside the sanctuary.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall take the bull of the sin offering, and it shall be burned in the appointed place of the house, outside the sanctuary.

verses.rationale: Keeps day, sex and ritual comparison.
verses.before: On the second day you will offer an unblemished male goat as a sin offering, and they will cleanse the altar from sin as they cleansed it with the bull.
verses.after: On the second day offer an unblemished male goat as a sin offering. They must purify the altar as they purified it with the bull.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the second day you shall offer an unblemished male goat as a sin offering, and they shall cleanse the altar from sin as they cleansed it with the bull.

verses.rationale: Retains both unblemished requirements.
verses.before: When you have finished cleansing it from sin, you will offer an unblemished bull from the herd and an unblemished ram from the flock.
verses.after: When you finish purifying it, offer an unblemished young bull and an unblemished ram from the flock.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you have finished cleansing it from sin, you shall offer an unblemished bull from the herd and an unblemished ram from the flock.

verses.rationale: Keeps salt and both divine names.
verses.before: You will bring them before the LORD. The priests will throw salt on them and offer them up as a burnt offering to the LORD.
verses.after: Present them before the LORD. The priests must throw salt on them and offer them as a burnt offering to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall bring them before the LORD. The priests shall throw salt on them and offer them up as a burnt offering to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves daily goat and additional animals.
verses.before: For seven days you will prepare a male goat as a sin offering each day; and they will prepare an unblemished bull from the herd and an unblemished ram from the flock.
verses.after: For seven days provide a male goat as a sin offering each day. They must also provide an unblemished young bull and an unblemished ram from the flock.
verses.tsw_comparator: For seven days you shall prepare a male goat as a sin offering each day; and they shall prepare an unblemished bull from the herd and an unblemished ram from the flock.

verses.rationale: Renders filling-hands idiom as consecration with note.
verses.before: For seven days they will make atonement for the altar, cleanse it, and consecrate it.
verses.after: For seven days they must make atonement for the altar, cleanse it, and consecrate it.
verses.tsw_comparator: For seven days they shall make atonement for the altar, cleanse it, and consecrate it.

verses.rationale: Keeps eighth-day transition and acceptance of people.
verses.before: When they have completed the days, from the eighth day onward the priests will offer on the altar your burnt offerings and your well-being offerings. Then I will accept you, declares the LORD GOD.”
verses.after: When these days are complete, from the eighth day onward the priests must offer your burnt offerings and your peace offerings on the altar. Then I will accept you, declares the Lord GOD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When they have completed the days, from the eighth day onward the priests shall offer on the altar your burnt offerings and your well-being offerings. Then I will accept you, declares the LORD GOD.”

verses.rationale: Retains location and closed state.
verses.before: Then he brought me back by way of the outer gate of the sanctuary, the one facing east; and it was shut.
verses.after: He brought me back to the sanctuary’s outer gate facing east. It was shut.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he brought me back by way of the outer gate of the sanctuary, the one facing east; and it was shut.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated closure and both divine names.
verses.before: And the LORD said to me, “This gate will remain shut. It will not be opened, and no one will enter through it, because the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered through it. Therefore it will remain shut.
verses.after: The LORD told me, “This gate must remain shut. It must not be opened, and no one may enter through it, because the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered through it. It must remain shut.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD said to me, “This gate shall remain shut. It shall not be opened, and no one shall enter through it, because the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered through it. Therefore it shall remain shut.

verses.rationale: Preserves prince's limited access and route.
verses.before: As for the prince, the prince himself may sit in it to eat bread before the LORD. He will enter by way of the gate’s vestibule, and by the same way he will go out.”
verses.after: The prince, because he is prince, may sit there to eat bread before the LORD. He must enter by the gate’s vestibule and leave the same way.”
verses.tsw_comparator: As for the prince, the prince himself may sit in it to eat bread before the LORD. He shall enter by way of the gate’s vestibule, and by the same way he shall go out.”

verses.rationale: Keeps north route and repeated divine name.
verses.before: Then he brought me by way of the north gate to the front of the house. I looked, and look, the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD; and I fell on my face.
verses.after: Then he brought me through the north gate to the front of the temple. I looked: the glory of the LORD filled the LORD’s temple. I fell facedown.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he brought me by way of the north gate to the front of the house. I looked, and behold, the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD; and I fell on my face.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated attention and entry/exit concern.
verses.before: The LORD said to me, “Mortal, set your heart on this. See with your eyes and hear with your ears all that I speak to you concerning all the statutes of the house of the LORD and all its instructions. Set your heart on the entrance of the house and on every exit of the sanctuary.
verses.after: The LORD told me, “Son of man, pay attention. Look with your eyes and listen with your ears to everything I tell you about all the statutes and instructions of the LORD’s temple. Pay attention to the temple’s entrance and every exit from the sanctuary.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to me, “Mortal, set your heart on this. See with your eyes and hear with your ears all that I speak to you concerning all the statutes of the house of the LORD and all its instructions. Set your heart on the entrance of the house and on every exit of the sanctuary.

verses.rationale: Keeps force of rebuke.
verses.before: Say to the rebellious house, to the house of Israel: Thus says the LORD GOD: Enough of all your abominations, house of Israel,
verses.after: Tell the rebellious house of Israel: This is what the Lord GOD says: Enough of all your abominations, house of Israel!
verses.tsw_comparator: Say to the rebellious house, to the house of Israel: Thus says the LORD GOD: Enough of all your abominations, house of Israel,

verses.rationale: Retains heart/flesh distinction and they broke pronoun.
verses.before: when you brought in foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in my sanctuary, profaning my house, when you offered my food—the fat and the blood. They broke my covenant along with all your abominations.
verses.after: You brought foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and flesh, into my sanctuary to profane my house while you offered my food, the fat and blood. They broke my covenant in addition to all your abominations.
verses.tsw_comparator: when you brought in foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in my sanctuary, profaning my house, when you offered my food—the fat and the blood. They broke my covenant along with all your abominations.

verses.rationale: Clarifies implied others without naming a class.
verses.before: You have not kept charge of my holy things, but you appointed others to keep charge of my sanctuary for you.
verses.after: You did not keep charge of my holy things. You appointed others to keep charge of my sanctuary in your place.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have not kept charge of my holy things, but you appointed others to keep charge of my sanctuary for you.

verses.rationale: Keeps exclusion's exact twofold qualification.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD GOD: No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, will enter my sanctuary—no foreigner who is among the people of Israel.
verses.after: “This is what the Lord GOD says: No foreigner uncircumcised in heart and flesh may enter my sanctuary, including any foreigner living among the Israelites.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD GOD: No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter my sanctuary—no foreigner who is among the people of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated straying and responsibility.
verses.before: But the Levites who went far from me when Israel went astray, who went astray from me after their idols, will bear their iniquity.
verses.after: But the Levites who went far from me when Israel strayed, who strayed from me after their idols, must bear their guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the Levites who went far from me when Israel went astray, who went astray from me after their idols, shall bear their iniquity.

verses.rationale: Keeps permitted duties despite exclusion from priestly approach.
verses.before: Yet they will serve in my sanctuary, having charge of the gates of the house and serving in the house. They will slaughter the burnt offering and the sacrifice for the people, and they will stand before them to serve them.
verses.after: They may serve in my sanctuary, attending the temple’s gates and serving in the temple. They will slaughter burnt offerings and sacrifices for the people and stand before them to serve them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet they shall serve in my sanctuary, having charge of the gates of the house and serving in the house. They shall slaughter the burnt offering and the sacrifice for the people, and they shall stand before them to serve them.

verses.rationale: Preserves stumbling block and oath gesture.
verses.before: Because they served them before their idols and became for the house of Israel a stumbling block of iniquity, therefore I have raised my hand against them, declares the LORD GOD, and they will bear their iniquity.
verses.after: Because they served the people before their idols and became a stumbling block of guilt for the house of Israel, I have raised my hand in an oath against them, declares the Lord GOD. They must bear their guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because they served them before their idols and became for the house of Israel a stumbling block of iniquity, therefore I have raised my hand against them, declares the LORD GOD, and they shall bear their iniquity.

verses.rationale: Keeps restriction and degrees of holiness.
verses.before: They will not draw near to me to serve as priests for me, nor to draw near to any of my holy things, to the most holy things. They will bear their disgrace and the abominations that they have done.
verses.after: They must not approach me to serve as priests or come near any of my holy things, the most holy things. They must bear their disgrace for the abominations they committed.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall not draw near to me to serve as priests for me, nor to draw near to any of my holy things, to the most holy things. They shall bear their disgrace and the abominations that they have done.

verses.rationale: Preserves continuing service assignment.
verses.before: Yet I will appoint them to keep charge of the house, for all its service and for all that is to be done in it.
verses.after: Yet I will put them in charge of the temple’s duties, all its service and everything done there.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I will appoint them to keep charge of the house, for all its service and for all that is to be done in it.

verses.rationale: Keeps Zadokite exception and specific offerings.
verses.before: “But the Levitical priests, the sons of Zadok, who kept charge of my sanctuary when the people of Israel went astray from me—they will draw near to me to serve me. They will stand before me to offer me fat and blood, declares the LORD GOD.
verses.after: “But the Levitical priests descended from Zadok, who kept charge of my sanctuary when the Israelites strayed from me, may approach me to serve me. They will stand before me to offer fat and blood, declares the Lord GOD.
verses.tsw_comparator: “But the Levitical priests, the sons of Zadok, who kept charge of my sanctuary when the people of Israel went astray from me—they shall draw near to me to serve me. They shall stand before me to offer me fat and blood, declares the LORD GOD.

verses.rationale: Preserves table and sanctuary access.
verses.before: They will enter my sanctuary, and they will draw near to my table to serve me, and they will keep my charge.
verses.after: They may enter my sanctuary and approach my table to serve me. They must keep my charge.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall enter my sanctuary, and they shall draw near to my table to serve me, and they shall keep my charge.

verses.rationale: Keeps clothing rule and service locations.
verses.before: When they enter the gates of the inner court, they will wear linen garments. No wool will come upon them while they serve at the gates of the inner court and within.
verses.after: When they enter the inner court’s gates, they must wear linen garments. They must wear no wool while serving at the inner court’s gates or inside the temple.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they enter the gates of the inner court, they shall wear linen garments. No wool shall come upon them while they serve at the gates of the inner court and within.

verses.rationale: Preserves specific garments and sweat restriction.
verses.before: They will have linen turbans on their heads and linen undergarments on their bodies. They will not gird themselves with anything that causes sweat.
verses.after: They must wear linen turbans on their heads and linen undergarments around their waists. They must not bind themselves with anything that causes sweat.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall have linen turbans on their heads and linen undergarments on their bodies. They shall not gird themselves with anything that causes sweat.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated court and transferable holiness concept.
verses.before: When they go out to the outer court, to the outer court where the people are, they will take off the garments in which they minister and leave them in the holy chambers. They will put on other garments, so that they do not communicate holiness to the people by their garments.
verses.after: When they go out to the outer court—to the outer court where the people are—they must remove their service garments and leave them in the holy chambers. They must put on other clothes, so they do not transmit holiness to the people through their garments.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they go out to the outer court, to the outer court where the people are, they shall take off the garments in which they minister and leave them in the holy chambers. They shall put on other garments, so that they do not communicate holiness to the people by their garments.

verses.rationale: Keeps both prohibited extremes and positive duty.
verses.before: They will not shave their heads or let their hair grow long; they will keep the hair of their heads trimmed.
verses.after: They must neither shave their heads nor let their hair grow long. They must keep their hair trimmed.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall not shave their heads or let their hair grow long; they shall keep the hair of their heads trimmed.

verses.rationale: Preserves limited setting of prohibition.
verses.before: No priest will drink wine when they enter the inner court.
verses.after: No priest may drink wine when entering the inner court.
verses.tsw_comparator: No priest shall drink wine when they enter the inner court.

verses.rationale: Keeps gender-specific rule and explicit exception.
verses.before: They will not take a widow or a divorced woman as wives, but only virgins from the offspring of the house of Israel; or they may take a widow who is the widow of a priest.
verses.after: They must not marry a widow or a divorced woman, but only a virgin of Israelite descent. They may, however, marry the widow of a priest.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall not take a widow or a divorced woman as wives, but only virgins from the offspring of the house of Israel; or they may take a widow who is the widow of a priest.

verses.rationale: Preserves two distinctions without conflating them.
verses.before: They will teach my people the difference between holy and common, and reveal to them the difference between unclean and clean.
verses.after: They must teach my people to distinguish the holy from the common and make known the difference between unclean and clean.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall teach my people the difference between holy and common, and make known to them the difference between unclean and clean.

verses.rationale: Retains judging, festivals and Sabbath duties.
verses.before: In a dispute they will stand to judge; they will judge it according to my judgments. They will keep my instructions and my statutes at all my appointed times, and they will keep my Sabbaths holy.
verses.after: In a dispute they must serve as judges and decide it according to my judgments. They must keep my instructions and statutes at all my appointed festivals and keep my Sabbaths holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: In a dispute they shall stand to judge; they shall judge it according to my judgments. They shall keep my instructions and my statutes at all my appointed times, and they shall keep my Sabbaths holy.

verses.rationale: Preserves full family exception list.
verses.before: They will not go near a dead person to defile themselves, except for a father or mother, son or daughter, brother, or sister who has not belonged to a man; for these they may defile themselves.
verses.after: A priest must not approach a dead person and become unclean, except for a father, mother, son, daughter, brother, or a sister who has not married.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall not go near a dead person to defile themselves, except for a father or mother, son or daughter, brother, or sister who has not belonged to a man; for these they may defile themselves.

verses.rationale: Keeps additional seven-day interval.
verses.before: After the priest’s purification, they will count seven days for him.
verses.after: After his cleansing, seven days must be counted for him.
verses.tsw_comparator: After the priest’s purification, they shall count seven days for him.

verses.rationale: Retains reentry offering and stated space.
verses.before: On the day he enters the holy place, into the inner court, to serve in the holy place, he will offer his sin offering, declares the LORD GOD.
verses.after: On the day he enters the holy place, the inner court, to serve there, he must offer his sin offering, declares the Lord GOD.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the day he enters the holy place, into the inner court, to serve in the holy place, he shall offer his sin offering, declares the LORD GOD.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated divine inheritance/possession contrast.
verses.before: “This will be their inheritance: I am their inheritance. You will give them no possession in Israel; I am their possession.
verses.after: “This will be their inheritance: I am their inheritance. Give them no landed possession in Israel; I am their possession.
verses.tsw_comparator: “This shall be their inheritance: I am their inheritance. You shall give them no possession in Israel; I am their possession.

verses.rationale: Preserves the three offerings and the binding herem dedication; the priestly assignment here does not itself require destruction.
verses.before: They will eat the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering. Everything devoted to destruction in Israel will be theirs.
verses.after: They may eat the grain offering, sin offering, and guilt offering. Everything irrevocably devoted in Israel will belong to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall eat the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering. Everything devoted to destruction in Israel shall be theirs.

verses.rationale: Keeps firstfruits, contributions and dough distinct.
verses.before: The first of all the firstfruits of everything, and every contribution from all your contributions, will belong to the priests. You will give the first of your dough to the priest, so that a blessing may rest on your house.
verses.after: The first of all firstfruits and every contribution you offer will belong to the priests. Give the priest the first portion of your dough, so a blessing may rest on your house.
verses.tsw_comparator: The first of all the firstfruits of everything, and every contribution from all your contributions, shall belong to the priests. You shall give the first of your dough to the priest, so that a blessing may rest on your house.

verses.rationale: Preserves both death categories and animal groups.
verses.before: The priests will not eat anything, bird or animal, that dies of itself or is torn by beasts.
verses.after: The priests must not eat any bird or animal that died naturally or was torn by beasts.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priests shall not eat anything, bird or animal, that dies of itself or is torn by beasts.

verses.rationale: Retains unsupplied unit and pinned ten thousand.
verses.before: When you allot the land as an inheritance, you will set aside an offering for the LORD: a holy portion from the land, twenty-five thousand in length and ten thousand in width. It will be holy throughout its entire boundary all around.
verses.after: “When you allot the land as an inheritance, set apart a holy contribution for the LORD, twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide. The entire area within its boundaries will be holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you allot the land as an inheritance, you shall set aside an offering for the LORD: a holy portion from the land, twenty-five thousand in length and ten thousand in width. It shall be holy throughout its entire boundary all around.

verses.rationale: Keeps sanctuary square and explicit cubit margin.
verses.before: Of this, there will be for the sanctuary a square five hundred by five hundred, with fifty cubits of open land around it.
verses.after: Within it, the sanctuary will occupy a square five hundred by five hundred, with fifty cubits of open land around it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Of this, there shall be for the sanctuary a square five hundred by five hundred, with fifty cubits of open land around it.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated dimensions and holiness.
verses.before: From this measurement you will measure a length of twenty-five thousand and a width of ten thousand. In it will be the sanctuary, the most holy place.
verses.after: From this measured area mark off a length of twenty-five thousand and a width of ten thousand. Within it will be the sanctuary, the Most Holy Place.
verses.tsw_comparator: From this measurement you shall measure a length of twenty-five thousand and a width of ten thousand. In it shall be the sanctuary, the most holy place.

verses.rationale: Keeps priestly service and housing distinct.
verses.before: It will be a holy portion from the land for the priests, the ministers of the sanctuary who draw near to minister to the LORD. It will be a place for their houses and a holy place for the sanctuary.
verses.after: This holy portion of the land will belong to the priests who serve in the sanctuary, who approach the LORD to serve him. It will provide space for their houses and a holy place for the sanctuary.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall be a holy portion from the land for the priests, the ministers of the sanctuary who draw near to minister to the LORD. It shall be a place for their houses and a holy place for the sanctuary.

verses.rationale: Retains pinned twenty chambers rather than cities.
verses.before: A length of twenty-five thousand and a width of ten thousand will belong to the Levites, the ministers of the house, as their possession: twenty chambers.
verses.after: A portion twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide will belong to the Levites who serve in the temple, as their possession, with twenty chambers.
verses.tsw_comparator: A length of twenty-five thousand and a width of ten thousand shall belong to the Levites, the ministers of the house, as their possession: twenty chambers.

verses.rationale: Keeps city dimensions and common ownership.
verses.before: Alongside the holy offering you will give the city a possession five thousand in width and twenty-five thousand in length. It will belong to the whole house of Israel.
verses.after: Give the city a possession five thousand wide and twenty-five thousand long, alongside the holy contribution. It will belong to the whole house of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Alongside the holy offering you shall give the city a possession five thousand in width and twenty-five thousand in length. It shall belong to the whole house of Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves extent without adding diagram assumptions.
verses.before: For the prince there will be land on both sides of the holy offering and of the city’s possession, alongside the holy offering and alongside the city’s possession, from the west side westward and from the east side eastward. Its length will correspond to one of the tribal portions, from the western boundary to the eastern boundary.
verses.after: The prince will have land on both sides of the holy contribution and the city’s possession, alongside them, extending westward on the west and eastward on the east. Its length will match one tribal portion, from the western boundary to the eastern boundary.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the prince there shall be land on both sides of the holy offering and of the city’s possession, alongside the holy offering and alongside the city’s possession, from the west side westward and from the east side eastward. Its length shall correspond to one of the tribal portions, from the western boundary to the eastern boundary.

verses.rationale: Keeps restriction tied to allotted possession.
verses.before: This will be his possession in Israel’s land, so that my princes will no longer oppress my people. They will give the land to the house of Israel according to their tribes.
verses.after: This land will be his possession in Israel. My princes will no longer oppress my people but will leave the land to the house of Israel according to their tribes.
verses.tsw_comparator: This shall be his possession in Israel’s land, so that my princes will no longer oppress my people. They shall give the land to the house of Israel according to their tribes.

verses.rationale: Preserves dispossession prohibition and both titles.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD GOD: Enough of you, princes of Israel! Put away violence and devastation; do justice and righteousness. Put an end to your expulsions of my people, declares the LORD GOD.
verses.after: “This is what the Lord GOD says: Enough, princes of Israel! Put away violence and plunder. Do what is just and right. Stop driving my people from their property, declares the Lord GOD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD GOD: Enough of you, princes of Israel! Put away violence and devastation; do justice and righteousness. Put an end to your expulsions of my people, declares the LORD GOD.

verses.rationale: Keeps three parallel standards.
verses.before: You will have just balances, a just ephah, and a just bath.
verses.after: Use honest scales, an honest ephah, and an honest bath.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall have just balances, a just ephah, and a just bath.

verses.rationale: Preserves equal dry/liquid capacities and repeated tenths.
verses.before: The ephah and the bath will have the same measure: the bath will contain one-tenth of a homer, and the ephah one-tenth of a homer. Their standard measure will be according to the homer.
verses.after: The ephah and the bath must have the same capacity: the bath one-tenth of a homer and the ephah one-tenth of a homer. The homer will be their standard.
verses.tsw_comparator: The ephah and the bath shall have the same measure: the bath shall contain one-tenth of a homer, and the ephah one-tenth of a homer. Their standard measure shall be according to the homer.

verses.rationale: Retains unusual additive sixty-shekel specification.
verses.before: The shekel will be twenty gerahs. Twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels, and fifteen shekels will be your mina.
verses.after: The shekel will be twenty gerahs. Twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels, and fifteen shekels will make your mina.
verses.tsw_comparator: The shekel shall be twenty gerahs. Twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels, and fifteen shekels shall be your mina.

verses.rationale: Keeps separate grain dues and exact fractions.
verses.before: This is the offering that you will set aside: one-sixth of an ephah from each homer of wheat, and one-sixth of an ephah from each homer of barley.
verses.after: “This is the contribution you must offer: one-sixth of an ephah from each homer of wheat and one-sixth of an ephah from each homer of barley.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the offering that you shall set aside: one-sixth of an ephah from each homer of wheat, and one-sixth of an ephah from each homer of barley.

verses.rationale: Retains cor/homer relationship and repeated equivalence.
verses.before: The prescribed portion of oil will be one-tenth of a bath from each cor of oil—the cor being ten baths, or one homer, since ten baths are a homer.
verses.after: The prescribed portion of oil, measured by the bath, is one-tenth of a bath from each cor. Ten baths make a homer, for a homer is ten baths.
verses.tsw_comparator: The prescribed portion of oil shall be one-tenth of a bath from each cor of oil—the cor being ten baths, or one homer, since ten baths are a homer.

verses.rationale: Keeps livestock rate and three offering categories.
verses.before: And one sheep from every two hundred from the well-watered pastures of Israel, for the grain offering, the burnt offering, and the well-being offerings, to make atonement for them, declares the LORD GOD.
verses.after: Take one sheep from every two hundred from Israel’s well-watered pastures. These will provide grain offerings, burnt offerings, and peace offerings to make atonement for them, declares the Lord GOD.
verses.tsw_comparator: And one sheep from every two hundred from the well-watered pastures of Israel, for the grain offering, the burnt offering, and the well-being offerings, to make atonement for them, declares the LORD GOD.

verses.rationale: Preserves collective contribution and recipient.
verses.before: All the people of the land will be responsible for this offering for the prince in Israel.
verses.after: All the people of the land must give this contribution to the prince in Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the people of the land shall be responsible for this offering for the prince in Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves complete repeated offering and occasion lists.
verses.before: The burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings at the festivals, new moons, Sabbaths, and all the appointed times of the house of Israel will be the prince’s responsibility. He will provide the sin offering, the grain offering, the burnt offering, and the well-being offerings, to make atonement for the house of Israel.
verses.after: The prince will be responsible for the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings at the feasts, new moons, Sabbaths, and all the house of Israel’s appointed festivals. He must provide the sin offering, grain offering, burnt offering, and peace offerings to make atonement for the house of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: The burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings at the festivals, new moons, Sabbaths, and all the appointed times of the house of Israel shall be the prince’s responsibility. He shall provide the sin offering, the grain offering, the burnt offering, and the well-being offerings, to make atonement for the house of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps date and animal requirement.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD GOD: In the first month, on the first day of the month, you will take a flawless young bull and purify the sanctuary from sin.
verses.after: “This is what the Lord GOD says: On the first day of the first month, take an unblemished young bull and purify the sanctuary.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD GOD: In the first month, on the first day of the month, you shall take a flawless young bull and purify the sanctuary from sin.

verses.rationale: Keeps three blood-application sites.
verses.before: The priest will take some of the blood of the sin offering and put it on the doorposts of the house, on the four corners of the altar’s ledge, and on the doorposts of the gate of the inner court.
verses.after: The priest must take some blood from the sin offering and put it on the temple’s doorpost, the four corners of the altar’s ledge, and the doorpost of the inner court’s gate.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering and put it on the doorposts of the house, on the four corners of the altar’s ledge, and on the doorposts of the gate of the inner court.

verses.rationale: Retains pinned seventh day rather than seventh month.
verses.before: You will do the same on the seventh day of the month for anyone who strays or acts unknowingly. Thus you will make atonement for the house.
verses.after: Do the same on the seventh day of the month for anyone who sins unintentionally or unknowingly. In this way you will make atonement for the temple.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall do the same on the seventh day of the month for anyone who strays or acts unknowingly. Thus you shall make atonement for the house.

verses.rationale: Keeps Passover date and contextual week duration.
verses.before: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, you will have the Passover, a festival lasting seven days. Unleavened bread will be eaten.
verses.after: On the fourteenth day of the first month, observe the Passover, a festival lasting seven days. Unleavened bread must be eaten.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, you shall have the Passover, a festival lasting seven days. Unleavened bread shall be eaten.

verses.rationale: Preserves ruler's inclusion among beneficiaries.
verses.before: On that day the prince will provide, for himself and for all the people of the land, a bull as a sin offering.
verses.after: On that day the prince must provide a bull as a sin offering for himself and all the people of the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day the prince shall provide, for himself and for all the people of the land, a bull as a sin offering.

verses.rationale: Keeps seven-by-seven daily schedule.
verses.before: During the seven days of the festival he will provide as a burnt offering to the LORD seven bulls and seven rams without blemish each day for the seven days, and a male goat each day as a sin offering.
verses.after: For each of the festival’s seven days he must provide a burnt offering to the LORD: seven unblemished bulls and seven unblemished rams each day, and a male goat each day as a sin offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: During the seven days of the festival he shall provide as a burnt offering to the LORD seven bulls and seven rams without blemish each day for the seven days, and a male goat each day as a sin offering.

verses.rationale: Preserves per-animal and per-volume ratios.
verses.before: He will provide a grain offering of an ephah for each bull and an ephah for each ram, with a hin of oil for each ephah.
verses.after: He must provide a grain offering of an ephah for each bull and an ephah for each ram, with a hin of oil for each ephah.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall provide a grain offering of an ephah for each bull and an ephah for each ram, with a hin of oil for each ephah.

verses.rationale: Retains second festival without supplying absent name.
verses.before: In the seventh month, on the fifteenth day of the month, at the festival, he will provide the same for the seven days: the same sin offering, burnt offering, grain offering, and oil.
verses.after: At the festival beginning on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, he must provide the same for seven days: sin offerings, burnt offerings, grain offerings, and oil.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the seventh month, on the fifteenth day of the month, at the festival, he shall provide the same for the seven days: the same sin offering, burnt offering, grain offering, and oil.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes inner gate from permanently shut outer gate.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD GOD: The gate of the inner court that faces east will be closed during the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it will be opened, and on the day of the new moon it will be opened.
verses.after: “This is what the Lord GOD says: The east-facing gate of the inner court must remain shut during the six working days. It must be opened on the Sabbath and on the new moon.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD GOD: The gate of the inner court that faces east shall be closed during the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened.

verses.rationale: Keeps priest/prince roles and gate timing.
verses.before: The prince will enter by way of the gate's vestibule from outside and stand by the doorpost of the gate. The priests will offer his burnt offering and his well-being offerings, and he will bow down at the threshold of the gate. Then he will go out, but the gate will not be closed until evening.
verses.after: The prince must enter from outside through the gate’s vestibule and stand beside the gatepost. The priests will offer his burnt offering and peace offerings. He must bow at the threshold and then leave, but the gate must remain open until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: The prince shall enter by way of the gate's vestibule from outside and stand by the doorpost of the gate. The priests shall offer his burnt offering and his well-being offerings, and he shall bow down at the threshold of the gate. Then he shall go out, but the gate shall not be closed until evening.

verses.rationale: Preserves people's place and occasions.
verses.before: The people of the land will bow down at the entrance of that gate before the LORD on the Sabbaths and new moons.
verses.after: On Sabbaths and new moons the people of the land must bow before the LORD at that gate’s entrance.
verses.tsw_comparator: The people of the land shall bow down at the entrance of that gate before the LORD on the Sabbaths and new moons.

verses.rationale: Keeps six/one and separate blemish requirements.
verses.before: The burnt offering that the prince presents to the LORD on the Sabbath day will be six unblemished lambs and an unblemished ram.
verses.after: The burnt offering the prince presents to the LORD on the Sabbath must be six unblemished lambs and one unblemished ram.
verses.tsw_comparator: The burnt offering that the prince presents to the LORD on the Sabbath day shall be six unblemished lambs and an unblemished ram.

verses.rationale: Preserves discretionary lamb amount.
verses.before: The grain offering will be an ephah for the ram, and for the lambs a grain offering as much as he can give, with a hin of oil for each ephah.
verses.after: The grain offering will be an ephah for the ram, and for the lambs whatever he gives, with a hin of oil for each ephah.
verses.tsw_comparator: The grain offering shall be an ephah for the ram, and for the lambs a grain offering as much as he is able to give, with a hin of oil for each ephah.

verses.rationale: Keeps all animals and repeated qualification.
verses.before: On the day of the new moon, it will be an unblemished young bull from the herd, six lambs, and a ram; they will be unblemished.
verses.after: On the new moon he must offer an unblemished young bull, six lambs, and a ram; they must be unblemished.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the day of the new moon, it shall be an unblemished young bull from the herd, six lambs, and a ram; they shall be unblemished.

verses.rationale: Retains ability-based provision and oil ratio.
verses.before: He will provide an ephah as a grain offering for the bull and an ephah for the ram, and for the lambs as much as he can give, with a hin of oil for each ephah.
verses.after: He must provide an ephah as a grain offering for the bull and an ephah for the ram. For the lambs he may give as much as he can, with a hin of oil for each ephah.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall provide an ephah as a grain offering for the bull and an ephah for the ram, and for the lambs as much as he is able to give, with a hin of oil for each ephah.

verses.rationale: Keeps ruler's prescribed route.
verses.before: When the prince enters, he will enter by way of the gate's vestibule, and he will go out by the same way.
verses.after: When the prince enters, he must come through the gate’s vestibule and leave the same way.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the prince enters, he shall enter by way of the gate's vestibule, and he shall go out by the same way.

verses.rationale: Preserves both reciprocal routes and prohibition.
verses.before: When the people of the land come before the LORD at the appointed times, whoever enters by way of the north gate to bow down will go out by way of the south gate; and whoever enters by way of the south gate will go out by way of the north gate. No one will return by way of the gate through which they entered, but will go out straight ahead.
verses.after: When the people of the land come before the LORD at the appointed festivals, whoever enters by the north gate to worship must leave by the south gate, and whoever enters by the south must leave by the north. No one may return by the gate they entered; they must leave by the opposite gate.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the people of the land come before the LORD at the appointed times, whoever enters by way of the north gate to bow down shall go out by way of the south gate; and whoever enters by way of the south gate shall go out by way of the north gate. No one shall return by way of the gate through which they entered, but shall go out straight ahead.

verses.rationale: Keeps final plural rather than flattening it.
verses.before: The prince will be among them: when they enter, he will enter; and when they go out, they will go out.
verses.after: The prince will be among them, entering when they enter; when they leave, they will go out together.
verses.tsw_comparator: The prince shall be among them: when they enter, he shall enter; and when they go out, they shall go out.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated festival ratios.
verses.before: At the festivals and appointed times, the grain offering will be an ephah for the bull and an ephah for the ram, and for the lambs as much as he can give, with a hin of oil for each ephah.
verses.after: At the feasts and appointed festivals, the grain offering will be an ephah for each bull and an ephah for each ram, and for the lambs whatever he gives, with a hin of oil for each ephah.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the festivals and appointed times, the grain offering shall be an ephah for the bull and an ephah for the ram, and for the lambs as much as he is able to give, with a hin of oil for each ephah.

verses.rationale: Keeps voluntary occasion and different closing time.
verses.before: When the prince provides a voluntary burnt offering or voluntary well-being offerings to the LORD, the gate that faces east will be opened for him. He will provide his burnt offering and his well-being offerings just as he does on the Sabbath day. Then he will go out, and the gate will be closed after he has gone out.
verses.after: When the prince makes a freewill offering to the LORD, a burnt offering or peace offerings, the east-facing gate must be opened for him. He will offer his burnt offering and peace offerings as on the Sabbath. Then he must leave, and the gate must be shut after him.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the prince provides a voluntary burnt offering or voluntary well-being offerings to the LORD, the gate that faces east shall be opened for him. He shall provide his burnt offering and his well-being offerings just as he does on the Sabbath day. Then he shall go out, and the gate shall be closed after he has gone out.

verses.rationale: Preserves age and repeated daily timing.
verses.before: You will provide an unblemished lamb a year old as a daily burnt offering to the LORD. Every morning you will provide it.
verses.after: “Provide an unblemished year-old lamb each day as a burnt offering to the LORD. Offer it morning by morning.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall provide an unblemished lamb a year old as a daily burnt offering to the LORD. Every morning you shall provide it.

verses.rationale: Keeps exact unequal fractions and enduring obligation.
verses.before: You will provide with it a grain offering every morning: one-sixth of an ephah, with one-third of a hin of oil to moisten the choice flour. This is a grain offering to the LORD, a permanent statute, continually.
